Note: I played this game for many, many hours using the non-Steam version, so the play time that you see above is not actually reflective of the total time that I have spent enjoying this game!
A very good historical RTS (real-time strategy) game that covers an era of history that is often overlooked in video games - roughly the time from the European Renaissance to about the 1860s (just after the Civil War in the United States of America). The game is much more historically "authentic" than its predecessor, Age of Empires 2 (which was set in the Middle Ages), because each civilization is now much more distinct, with its own architectural style and many more unique units that are special to that civilization alone.
Personally, I love the new historical setting of Age of Empires 3! I just really enjoy starting in the Renaissance with units that wield mostly swords, spears, shields, crossbows, and only a few gunpowder weapons (arquebusiers and early cannons), and then evolving my civilization all the way to advanced riflemen, bombard cannons, mortar teams, and ironclad warships.
The main new feature in the game is that of the "Home City", which is a sort of capital city for your empire from which you can summon unit reinforcements, resource supplies, and special abilities to aid in your battles. Also, you can force alliances with local neutral factions on the game map that can provide with further unique units, upgrades, and powers.
Overall, Age of Empires 3 is much more fast-paced than its predecessors, something that you may or may not like depending on your play-style in RTS games. The battles usually start earlier in the game and are much more intense than in Age of Empires 2, but there is also less "grand" strategy as in that older game. Basically, Age of Empires 3 is more focused on the micromanagement of individual clashes on the field of battle, rather than on the broader macromanagement of the resources of a sprawling empire. Personally, I do not mind this shift in strategic perspective; when I want to play a "larger" game, I can always go back to Age of Empires 2 (now, in an HD Edition here on Steam), but when I want a more intense experience, I prefer Age of Empires 3.
I should also mention the graphics and sound design. Simply - both are absolutely superb! Although it is true that the graphical textures are pretty bad when you zoom-in very close, from a distance everything looks truly gorgeous. The cannons smoke from the explosions of gunpowder and emit thundering "booms" when firing at the enemy; the water looks "liquid", and it reflects the sunlight; the sails and flags of ships wave back and forth in the winds. The overall presentation really cements the immersion in the battles and the historical setting.
The campaign is, unfortunately, the weakest point of the game because the story departs from the historical set-piece battles of Age of Empires 2; the storyline instead tries to tell a unique "pseudo-historical" tale of intrigue and conspiracy with its own fictional characters (something like out of a thriller novel by Dan Brown), but it just lacks adequate character development or compelling writing. Nevertheless, it is fairly lengthy, and the actual mission objectives for the various scenarios are well-designed, challenging (but fair), and overall fun to play.
You can also play skirmish battles against the computer outside of the campaign mode. The interesting aspect of these skirmish battles is that you can earn "experience points" as you play matches and upgrade your Home City as you progress, thereby unlocking new units and upgrades for any future skirmishes.
The online community for this game here on Steam is small, but still quite active and friendly, so playing online multiplayer is usually easy and enjoyable, although I must say that I do not have much experience with this side of the game, since I am normally a more singleplayer-oriented gamer. The multiplayer matches play out similarly to the computer skirmishes, in that you can upgrade your Home City as you play more and more games (your Home City for multiplayer is stored in your online account).
In conclusion, I have to say that I really have enjoyed Age of Empires 3 as much, if not actually more, than any of its predecessors or contemporaries. Although the singleplayer campaign is not quite a complete success, for me this game is just a deeply immersive and intense historical RTS game. I love the feeling of progression that I can get whenever I level-up and upgrade my Home City, and I really adore the vast number of special and unique units that can become available to your civilization as you explore the map or interact with your Home City.
My only hope and wish for Age of Empires 3 going forward is that maybe the Steam Workshop will be opened up for it in the future, so that we can access and easily install some of the great mods that have been created by the fan community for the game over the years since its release.

This game is already a bit old and definitely it looks old. If you don't care about graphics that much it's the best bus simulator out there.
I was a bus driver myself and I must admit this game feels very realistic. In my life I was lucky to be able to pilot a plane and drive a train but I think this game gives the best feel of all transport simulator available. We also have realistic traffic (which is sometimes unfortunately a bit bugged) which is so essential to every city simulation game. What I really like to do is to learn a route and then drive it like in real life for whole day. There are no limitations - we can take out a bus early from the yard, drive it whole day according to the schedule and then take it back. Of course we can save the game and don't have to do it in one try. If we get bored we can instantly jump to another bus on another route or put a new bus into any place ourselves.
There are lot's of freeware add-ons both in terms of routes and busses. Therefore we can drive Solaris, MAN, Ikarus and many different models. There are great freeware routes (many of them are better than payware) both realistic and fictional so plenty to chose from.
The game has some limitations. The pedestrains sometimes behave weird, sometimes a car will bump into you without your fault but in general when we get to know these things we can start to ignore them. Good steering wheel is highly recommended for this game. Remember it's a simulator not a simple arcade. We really need a good feel of the wheel to fit these large busses into sharp corners. Still if you don't own a wheel, mouse playing is pretty effective. I do it often myself on the laptop when I don't want to take a wheel with me :) I don't recommend steering by keyboard.
To summarise - it's a great simulator with a lot's of routes and buses to chose from. But it lacks modern graphics and sometimes traffic doesn't work as intended.

If you're used to FPS games like I am with instant results and a wide margin for messing up (Titanfall, KF, Wildlands, etc.: gota problem? Explode their asses), then the DS series is going to make you rage.
The learning curve for switching to melee based combat with many different movesets for each weapon can be steep. The enemies are unforgiving in the damage they dish out. Even at a level 60 you can still be quickly killed by beginning game enemies if you wanted to.
I love/hate this game and the fact that I just can't stop playing it says a lot about its ability to keep players engaged despite its super frustrating and inevitable seemingly-endless dying.
I have learned to be much more patient with it than I usually am with games because that is so much more rewarding.
For example, there are these vicious killer crocodile creatures who are super fast, lunge attacks, spin attacks, one-hit kill you and I just could not beat them until I took off all my fancy armor, took off my shield and just used a two handed stance with a Dark Sword imbued with fire. Killed it first try lol.
I'm using a keyboard and mouse and have no issues with keybinding what I need (the walk bind is a little awkward but I rarely use it).
The graphic scenery is amazing, the atmosphere and environment are just top-notch, I can't think of any other game out there that can compare. Its positives far outweigh any negatives in frustration I experienced and once I got past the learning cure, I was definitely enjoying myself a lot.
Oh, I also found it a lot easier than DS2 not sure if it's becase DS2 was my training wheels for DS3 or if DS2 is actually harder. I rage quit DS2 and have yet to finish it (xb1) lol

Although this is (or will be) a free to play game, their development priorities seem far from where they should be.  They seem to be focused on the art design of the game in their dev blogs, when gameplay and mechanics are far from finalized. This is especially frustrating for current supporters of the game, when we are expecting progress towards a more complete game and they continue to release more skins (microtransactions) to seemingly milk out their already limited player base. When this is a game regarded as a paid early access alpha and you prioritize microtransactions, you aren't selling an early access game but instead a final product, and this game is far from finalized. With these thoughts in mind here's the pros and cons:
Pros:
-excellent graphics and effects
Cons:
-Poor game balance (Certain ships are entirely outclassed by other ships)
-Endless Microtransactions
-Toxic and limited playerbase (The game's only major clan, He3, is present in most games and do not provide the healthiest of conversations to say the least)
-Ban-happy Developers*
* I mention this, because of a few cases that I know of where bans have been issued for seemingly no reason or justification. Especially when this is supposedly in early access development, I find it extremely disturbing that a company would focus on banning players to protect it's player base of at best 200 people from petty arguments during a match.
In conclusion, this game would be wildly successful if the developers get their priorities straight. But as of now it doesn't look like this will happen and I suggest staying away from this game.
*In response to the Developer's comment*
The "Intentionally Impersonating to cause disruption" was simply a name change that was satirical in nature towards this particular clan, especially for their notable regard for being extremely negative in games. No other provacation was done, and simply changing the steam username was enough to recieve an immense amount of harassment from these members, and to my surprise later lead to a no-warning ban of my account which was noticed after about a week of inactivity. I mention in my review that others have been banned for "seemingly no reason" because, as per further investigation, many other former players recieved similar bans for reasons that they were unable to identify. In my own case, it was simply from a single name change that criticized this player organization. Absolutely no profanity or derogative language was used at all.
To further illustrate a point, the fact that a community representitive has taken the time to single out one player's review of this game (Out of 1500 reviews), shows their desperate attempt to clear out any possible criticism of this game, especially since the response is " This guy was banned, don't listen to him.". Take from this reveiw what you will, but I would not have such a negative view of this game if it wasn't for the  poor management from the developers in many different regards, not just in terms of my own case.

Once more we need a ‘meh’ button.  Starbound is a beautiful game with incredible music, fantastic graphics and a lot of fun to be had.  That said, the controls are a bit loose, the gameplay is repetitive and there’s not much to do.  This is early access so I’m being generous, and I do recommend it, but only if you mod it.  There’s no real goal in the game, no bosses to fight, no quests to be done, and after a while you get tired of going to new planets, depleting the resources and moving on.  I get more fun writing fanfics about my little person zipping through space from planet to planet, putting right what once went wrong and hoping each time that her next leap will be the leap home than I do playing, so I do get some enjoyment out of it.  But the game is still early access and there’s time for them to add a deeper storyline, quests, bosses and so forth.  Seven stolen cheese wheels out of ten.
Edit: April, 2015.  I haven't played in a while, so I loaded it up to see what changed.  Quite a lot, actually!  They added a starting quest line-tutorial and more of a story.  Eight and half stolen cheese wheels out of ten.
Edit: June 20, 2015.  I grew really frusterated with the game and quit early May, then started again mid-June.  The difficultly is all over the place now.  The mining boss is a bit too hard and almost not fun, and I STILL haven't gotten that danged penguin downed.  I'm trying again since they updated again, but it really needs to be balanced.  I'm taking back a cheese wheel and a half, back to seven.  Actually, make it six- we need a save point to teleport to before each boss.
Edit: November 18, 2017
The game has really become a thing of beauty, all the major issues I have with it are fixed, and it needs no modding to be a great game.  Ten out of ten stolen cheese wheels.

Assassins creed unity, with its poor launch and multiple glitches, is in fact the best game of the year in my opinion.
Hearing of all the performance issues from others, I was a bit worried when buying this game. Unsure whether I got really really lucky, I was able to play this game just fine.
My specs:
i5 4670k @ 4.4ghz
8gb ddr3 ram
GTX 970 OC edition from Asus.
I have been running this game like a dream. Averaging around 55 fps with all settings at highest besides aa. I realize that many people have been struggling to hit even 10fps with near super computers which is definately an issue to be fixed. With that being said I will now give my opinion on what I think of the game so far, starting with the cons of the game itsself, and not of the performance. I believe that this will be the best game of the year if Ubisoft can get back on their feet and slow down a bit.
Cons-
Enemy ai can be a bit funny sometimes, such as an enemy following you halfway across Paris even if you're miles away.
A texture pops in a little more than I would like to see in a AAA game.
Pause menu's are a little laggy at times.
I have heard others complain of the long loading times, although I don't experience anything more than about 20 seconds.
Obviously those are just my cons as I'm sure others would find many more than I did. I am not a fanboy of this series, I have only owned Assassin's creed 2 and 4, and I loved both of them. With that out of the way, now the Pros.
Pros-
Paris...This city is stunning, the shadows, reflections, textures, everything is simply breathtaking, I believe that this game has jumped the gap between Last and Next gen gaming, truly maximizing the visuals to something we've never seen in a game.
The new combat system is a very...very good jump from Black flag, instead of pressing 2 keys (counter-attack) I am now finding myself forced to use more stealth simply for the fact of it being impossible to face an army like in past games.
The story, without spoiling too much, Arno is pretty much a disrespectful, cocky young man who finds it hard to respect well?....anyone. The story is longer than any story I've played in the series with enough side missions to keep you occupied for a good year or two.
The new parkour engine is very well done, making transitions smoother and more fluid. As any game though, your character tends to grab the wrong window when you need to make that fast escape resulting in a lot of anger at times.
The accessability. Simply stunning, 1 out of 4 homes is fully accessable and furnished with even the tiniest details such as silverware. It is things like these that Truly immerse people the most, making it feel just a little closer to actually being there.
The character customization is very well done. I was a bit sceptical at first but I love being able to make my own truly unique assassins when playing with friends.
The multiplayer. From what I have played of it, It is very well made and seamless. Being able to play with 4 people in a sandbox the size of Paris is simply incredible. This should hold me over till GTA V in terms of free roaming.
So thats about it, I probably sounded biased in the Pros but those were just the things that I personally enjoyed. I wish I could give it a full 10 stars but for the bad release that many experienced I will be giving it a 9/10. This game is like nothing we've seen before, truly utilizing the power of next gen to bring us a game that is well worth the 60$. I hope I didnt offend anyone in this, I simply saw all the worthless reviews going around and felt like people should know the REAL facts about the games.

It is really hard to actually Recommend the game which was fairly mediocre even 10 years back. On the other hand, we live in the world where even mediocre titles from year 2005 are looking more original, than so many "new" releases...
This review is not an invintation to buy the game - even on the sale it may not worth the sport. Yet I think that Bet on Soldier is worth to be remembered, if not for gameplay, then at least for amount of catchy features, that actually worked in the game.
While the main character motivation is too sketchy to be of any interest, the layout, the world of BoS - that's another story. In this world, the Grand War, started at 1914, was never ceased. It mutated from states rival for colonies to struggle of global corporations for markets and minds... with bigger and bigger guns. And by the end of the century, the war evolved into TV show, with soldiers acting as gladiators, challenging one another on the deathmatch - under the cameras spotlights. And you know what? It sounds like a nice job for this grieving world.
You starting a level, picking yourself weapons of choice (whatever your money can buy) and enemies to fight against. Once you're on the mission, there are no medikits... instead, there are plenty of vending machines all around, to fix your armor and sell you more clips. And even for savepoint there is a special tax - which is quite an interesting move, which I actually liked - if you want more money, quit your "saving often" instincts, and try to actually stay alive longer... Ah, yeah, talking about FPS instincts - once you reloaded the clip, you lose it - with all ammo that was left there. And NO, you can't take clips or weapons from your enemies - only buy new ones with cash... Of course, these "features" with chargeable saves and ammo are not all fun... but quite ironic, as I see things.
Now, to more serious matters - like the opponents you choose to fight - all of them are wearing various power armors and tricky armaments, like the bullets and grenades with hallucinogens, which makes you go all blur... best to avoid, of course. Generally, those punks not only much tougher and challenging than usual cannon fodder, they are also a good prize to claim! To buy yourself a new heavy-barrelled toy afterwards, of course.
And, finally, after strange world of never ending war, twisting economical part (basically, you need to shoot and die less, kill with headshots - more), there goes large-scale battle operations! Including - surprise! - Mechas!
So, you may think of BoS as of MechWarriors2 - only newer, and with many missions on-foot. Or as of Lost Planet: Extreme Condition, only without grappling hook, and... older. Or like C&C Renegade... jeez, I'm starting to sound like an old-timer.
As of summary, I don't recommend to buy it - unless you're really deep into FPS games, and tired of modern titles like another CoD or Battlefield, and want to get something different. Of course, Bet on Soldier is not the nicest pick. Even with many interesting features it lacks intensity and even integrity sometimes. However, in my book it deserves 6/10 mark and thumbs up.

I would highly recommend you stay away from Fallout 4 for a 4 main reasons.
1. The entire game is focused on gunplay and will very rarely have any quests with choice or diplomacy involved. It's also oversaturated with copy and paste quests with objectives that boil down to "kill x amount of enemies" or "retrieve x by doing a dungeon". Combat encounters are also not interesting because there are only a handful of enemy types and 90% of them just shoot you, which means the only thing that separates a radier from a super mutant is how much you have to shoot them. The gunplay may be better than it's predecessors but it's not enough to hold up an entire game.
2. The writing and quests are incredibly bland. Even though the game has "4 endings" it only truly has 2 ending states. 1 is blowing up the evil scientists and 2 is siding with the evil scientists. If you're a long time fallout fan you should know that in just about every fallout game previous you would get a complex ending depending on what actions you did in many parts of the game. You only get rewarded with one prerendered cutscene which is basically the protagonist talking about everything you already know, things completely unrelated, and saying that "war never changes" in the end. I should also mention that you have a voiced protagonist, less dialouge options (yes, yes, explain, and sarcastic yes). You also have no skills, tag skills, traits, or even skill checks, which takes the RP out of RPG.
3. No character buliding. Since they've done away with stats and the like all the rpg elements are resigned to your special stats and the "perks" that go along with them. Perks do not function as they have in any other fallout game because they not serve the purpose of having a leveling system. Every level you get 1 perk point to put into any of the perks you have available. But you'll end up ignoring most of the semi-interesting ones to put it into gunplay or modding your weapons, because almost all of the quests invole shooting people. The way they make you upgrade your weapons skills is also very annoying. Your weapon upgrades are not based around making weapons types better (guns, energy weapons, melee, unarmed) but having the upgrades only effect certain weapon firing types (auto, semi-auto, etc) which sucks any variety the gunplay still could have had. That means if you found a really cool gun you can only viably use it if it fires the way that corresponds with what you put your perk points into. It's confusing for new players, and annoying for all players.
4. Bloatware and Paid Mods. For those unaware bloatware is a type of software that takes up a large amount of hard drive space. And with the new paid mods it earns that title. Because their new paid mod initiative (that is patched into every game now) installs all of the mods that are available to purchase, your harddrive is going to be full with useless data. Not to mention that paid mods are one of the scummiest things to come out in a long time. I don't think bethesda understands that mods are made out of love for a game, not to bleed consumers dry. Even if you're ok with everything above I wouldn't buy this game because you'd be supporting this terrible buisness practice.
I would not recommend anybody play this game. With the 60 dollars this game costs you could buy every other game in the fallout series. If you're more of a fan of shooter games buy the new DOOM, it's miles better than this and you can even make your own levels with their snapmap mode. And if you want to play the settlement mode (that isn't even worth mentioning) just ♥♥♥♥ing buy Minecraft, it's a fraction of the cost and updates are free. Go buy yourself a nice dinner or 10 of everything mcdonalds value menu, because you'll get more enjoyment out of that than playing Fallout 4.
TL;DR: Gameplay is boring, writing is bland, it has paid mods, it's bloatware, go buy something else.

Initial impressions - sound design is meh. Animations and graphics are dated, as to be expected since the game was released in 2005.
Controls are weird; if you've been running and let off the W key, you will sometimes stop immediately and other times you will slide about 5 feet. This seems to happen no matter what terrain you are on.
some of the special powers are also stupid. Guns that blind you whenever you get hit seem like a cool idea right when you start, but in order to get your vision back you need to stop getting hit, which requires cover, which you can't find since you're blind. The hallucinogen grenades are ♥♥♥♥ing stupid. "Let's give an AoE attack that some bosses can spam that is even more frustrating than the blind guns because you can see you just will never be able to accurately shoot."
There is a huge weapon imbalance as well. There is no reason to run with an AR or Commando rifle, since the SMG's seem to have better accuracy, more damage, and a higher magazine capacity (which is greatly important for this game, since a mag you drop, even if you only fired one round out of it, is GONE until you get a chance to buy more ammo). The sniper rifles as a class are also obscenely strong; you can two shot anyone except the most heavily armored mooks with headshots. Those heavy armor mooks take 3, while it will take multiple MAGAZINES to spray down those heavy armored mooks with an AR/Commando rifle.
Shooting mechanics. Standard FPS, although for whatever stupid reason your zoom function is bound to your mousewheel click. Snipers are overpowered (in your hands, not the AI. The AI snipers suck) not just in terms of damage they deal, but also because this game seems to have some compensation for where you aim with the snipers, at least at the difficulty I played at. Several times, I would be aiming high chest and I would get headshot kills. I probably got more headshots like that than I did actually aiming at the head. Object hitboxes also tend to be weird, and you often can't tell until you've fired a shot into a clear area that it was actually an invisible wall.
All in all, I ended up ragequitting at stage 7. Not because the game was hard, but because a few minor irritants and one major one all added up to the game not being fun to play.
3/10, would NOT recommend.

What makes Black Squad better than all the other F2P shooter games out there?
In my review I'll talk about the pros and cons of BlackSquad and write a short recommendation if it is worth downloading for you.
pros:
-the f2p model is fantastic, it's quite comparable to League of Legends' f2p model, all you can buy are skins and unlock guns faster
-no guns with bonus stats, even the paid ones have literally the same stats as the free guns
-rewards for logging in. There is a monthly attendance deck and daily/weekly quests. The monthly deck does not reset, even if you don't log in every day and you get a fair amount of gold just for logging in (with just the log in reward you can buy a gun every week, without playing)
-enough starting money for two guns + free guns for 15 days if you download the DLCs (they are free)
-camping ain't an issue here, the time to kill someone is just low enough to keep it fast paced, and high enough to react
-very few cheaters. Cheating is a problem in shooter games and most f2p shooters are pested with cheaters. This one is the exception, I didn't encounter a single (blatant) cheater so far
-runs on a potato, but has a 144hz mode
neutral:
-most guns come with an equiped red dot and grenade launcher and there is no way to demount them
-swapping to your knife makes you sprint, there is no other way to sprint
-RNG spray patterns. Personally I like it, but there are a fair amount of people complaining about it
cons:
-the community. It's not really toxic, but it feels like there is no communication between the players. It's not like you have to talk to your teammates, but it feels like you are playing alone most of the time, thus once in a blue moon you meet players who are pretty nice to play with
-lack of gamemodes. The game is still in the early stages and is still developing, but I wish there were more gamemodes that give variety
-lack of a competetive scene. What's the point of ranks when all you have to do is spending time to get a higher level? I end up as #1 player in my games, but my rank doesn't really display my skill. Seeing players with really high ranks who are performing worse than me is kind of bothersome, since they don't really deserve a high rank, all they did is spending lots of time
Should you play it?
Perhaps. If you are into casual shooters that don't require lots of time to get good and have fun then yes. You don't have to spend a single penny to compete with spenders.
If you want a pure/realistic shooter like Battlefield 2, you won't be satisfied, it's still worth a shot, though.
tl;dr: Decent game for players who don't play frequently and want to have fun without spending money. I'd rate it 7/10.

My first Dark Souls game. I have much to read regarding the lore but here's my review on a new player trying to appreciate Dark Souls franchise on a computer with a mouse and keyboard.
The Good:
+ Incredible character design and detail
+ Incredible environment and locations
+ Incredible equipment and item designs
+ Locations are fun to explore
+ Incredible sound design and music
+ Very immersive from a visual and aural perspective
The Bad
- Camera is messy and annoying, especially when staying close to a wall. As a PC player, I don't like the "lock on the target" that console players prefer.
- Button remapping does not change on screen cue. Is it too much to ask?
- Button combos are weird. It feels exremely console-ish.
The Ugly
--- I appreciate the difficulty design decision, but it is way out of proportion. The enemies aren't smart by any way, just with unlimited stamina and wallhack.
--- Emenies attack with only one or two ways. There are no tactical decisions.
--- The physics are ♥♥♥♥ed up. Projectiles follow you and they will curve if you run sideways. OK, magic projectiles are fine, but arrows? bolts? Really?
--- The hitboxes are messed up even if you and the enemy aren't on the same level/ground. Sometimes the longer swords give you a longer reach illusion.
--- If I release sprint button mid-air, I would expect the character continues the sprint until it lands. Unfortunately the game does not think so.
--- If I press attack twice, sometimes the game registers as two attacks, sometimes it doesn't. Make the input window more sensible.
Did I have fun? Somewhat. I spent too much time dealing with the game mechanics than I expected. I have the feeling that I missed some stuff in the story line constantly because I have to divert my mind frequently into mechanics. Once I get the mechanics then I found out many things that will take the immersion away as I mentioned above.
TL;DR, A visually pleasing game marred by cryptic game mechanics and lazy AI-design decisions. Treat it as an interactive visual novel is a way to avoid disappointments. The game is not hard at all, it's just the game mechanics leave you tiny input windows to give you the illusion of being "difficult." Personally, the mechanics can be loosen quite a bit, and improve on the AI, i.e. make sensible and varied attack patterns.
Do I recommend this game? No.

I absolutely love this game; they recently reset the servers for what I think is the last time, but in all honesty I could play this game a thousand times from the beginning and still find pleasure in something new.
I love getting immersed in the intense space-combat; the graphics are awesome, the sound effects are traditional space-noises (just listen to a ship boosting, it's perfection) and the two styles of gameplay are enough to keep me interested.
The best thing about this game though is the support; if you've got an issue a dev will personally respond to your email, they'll offer step-by-step assistance and keep you updated on the steps to take to solve it. And best of all, the solution never takes more than a day. They just get their game, and they know how to make it work. They even play in-game with the other players, and are active in chat.
Sure, the game has some issues - currently DC'd players (deliberate rage quitters) wont get replaced by an active player so you're 1 team member down but this gives all team players a 30% respawn increase so I guess there's a bit of an upside, the styles of ship are different but incorporate into game play well. There's no "one ship" to rule the skies with, they all have weaknesses and strengths, and the care the devs have put into each ship is noticeable. It is a perfectly crafted game.
Now, luckily I got this game for free (I think?) when it was in the initial stages so I've grown with the game and learnt about it as I've gone along - the newsletter is a great read and I always look forward to snapshots of the new ships and ideas - but Id be happy to pay for this game if I was asked to. It is definitely worth the money for the quality you get, and whilst there are in-game purchases for platinum (quick-purchase ships and upgrades) you really don't need them to play the game all the way through. And you'll enjoy earning the 1.1m credits for the top ship in each faction. Honestly, you will.

Initially, the game simple crashed constantly and the frame rate was horrible.  It was unplayable.  While my graphic drivers were up to date, I tried reinstalling them and that fixed all of my problems.
The game generally is above 50 fps with a 780.
I generally don't write reviews but I want to address the plethora of complaints I am seeing.
Bugs: all games have bugs.  After reinstalling my graphic cards, I have seen 1 instance of bugs in roughly 8 hours of play.  It had no impact on the game.
Frame rates: the game is advertised as being very demanding.  They made a game that pushes modern tech.  That is a good thing.  It means if you feel like coming back to the game 2 years from now, it will still be beautiful.  If you do not yet have the hardware to play it on max settings but really want to enjoy it that way, sorry but that is your problem and not a fault with the game.
Parkour changes:  They changed it.  You now have an up and down option. It takes a bit to adjust but it's undeniably a smoother experience with far more control.  I believe the vast majority of complaints are simply people not adjusting well to a new system.
Yes, they botched the launch.  No, it's not a horrible game.
However, I don't particularly like some of the story/style changes.  It is more about stealth and less and less about combat.  It's a bit more niche.
The graphics are gorgeous.  However, some of the characters get in to uncanny valley territory.  They look just realistic enough that the flaws become creepy at times.
If you liked assassin's creed 1, 2 or 3, I would definitely recommend this game.  If you liked the pirate aspect of IV, you may not like this game.

Writing this review saddens me. I have been a fan of Bethesda’s games since Morrowind, which, like Oblivion, I bought twice (once in a store and once on Steam). My opinion of Bethesda was so positive that I preordered both Fallout 4 and the season pass. I trusted Bethesda enough to pay money for a game that had not been released yet. To date, that is the only time I have preordered a game. That is how much respect I had for Bethesda.
Fallout 4 itself is a good, but disappointing game. As I played it, I thought, “Man, I wish they had done more here,” far too often. For example, in the scene with Nick Valentine at the end of the Dangerous Minds quest, Bethesda hinted that continuing to travel with Nick might be a bad idea. That is why I kept him around. And I was disappointed. Nick went back to being just Nick. Bethesda hinted at a possible source of tension, a potential reason for the player to become invested in the story, and then they dropped it.
They did the same thing with Cait’s storyline. Rather than telling the story of a junkie’s slow and painful road to recovery, they invented a magical machine that cured her drug addiction forever. No tension. No reason to care.
And again with Piper. Talking with her reveals that she is worried that her younger sister will turn out to be just like her. But consoling Piper is enough to belay her fears. All the tension is gone. No reason to care. Another opportunity Bethesda wasted.
Et cetera. Et cetera.
Despite this, I still enjoyed Fallout 4. Bethesda’s greatest attribute has always been it’s ability to create amazing worlds. And the world of Fallout 4 is amazing - once you decide to ignore Preston Garvey and his idiotic radiant quests and just wander around the Commonwealth, that is. When you ditch all quests and just get lost in the world, Fallout 4 shines. The world Bethesda created in Fallout 4 tells a story far better than any of their quests do. There is a moment in every Bethesda game where I think, “Alright, show me something I have not seen before.” And Bethesda has never failed to do just that.
But, and this is a big but, finding that moment in Fallout 4 was harder than in any other Bethesda game. They seemed to be doing their utmost to keep players from wandering too far from their vision for the game. You can try to do your own thing, but the main questline will keep getting in your way. For example, completing Curie’s quest without first doing the Main Quest Dangerous Minds is impossible without using the console.
It feels as if Bethesda, for some insane reason, decided that it alone knew what players wanted. And if anyone dared to question their decisions (even the players themselves), then he/she was just wrong. Think about everything Bethesda has done since the release of Fallout 4...the mess that surrounded the unveiling of their mod service (I left the name out on purpose)...the underwhelming content provided in the beta release of their “club” (name omitted on purpose, any advertising is good advertising)...Bethesda thinking that it was okay to download this paltry collection of “curated” content onto people’s computers without being purchased… These are the actions of a company that has lost touch with it’s community, a community that turned Bethesda into the success it is.
This is why I cannot recommend Fallout 4. This is why Bethesda needs to repair the damage it has done to it’s community before I will buy another one of it’s games. They managed to turn this loyal fan into a cynic. Only Bethesda can remedy this. But I doubt they care. That is how low my opinion of them has fallen.

- cute comic style
- traditional path-based tower defence game
- loads of pop-culture references to films like Star Wars, Indiana Jones, Castaway, Predator etc.
- maps can change in the middle of the action when enemies create new paths
- challenging
- cool boss enemies that can make your whole defence setup worthless
- three difficulty levels plus Iron and Heroic difficulty with completely different waves of enemies
- more than 40 types of enemies
- complex combination of towers with different special abilities
- special attacks
- nine different heroes with very different special abilities
- looks and plays like the original - yes, that's a good thing
- addictive
- maps contain secrets
- upgradeable towers base values
- upgradeable heroes base values
- no glitches, no bugs
Cons:
- absolutely none

10/10

I simply loved "Kingdom Rush", for me it was one of the best tower defense games I've ever played. Therefore, I was no question whether I'd buy its sequel "Kingdom Rush Frontiers" immediately.
In the following I will consider some of the, in my opinion, key aspects of the game in detail.
Gameplay:
First, let me sum up the basics of the game: There are 4 types of towers, with 2 final branches each. There is a total of 15 levels, divided into 3 different regions with different types of enemies respectively. Each level has a "Heroic" and an "Iron" version that will unlock after the level was completed with perfect 3 stars. There are many different heroes that you can level up. Moreover you can also level up your powers and abilities with perks. That means you cannot only gear up your towers during a level but also globally.
All in all, the different towers, abilities and heroes form a unique gameplay. Especially the abilities and the heroes are features that I missed in so many other TD games, and that make this game so great, in my opinion.
Graphics:
The graphics of this game simply look gorgeous. Every pixel looks like it was handcrafted affectionately.
The price with respect to the content:
10 bucks for initially 15 levels and ~20 hours of fun; sounds okay to me (note: I think that I completed the game quickly). But wait, there's more: Shortly after the release of the game the devs announced 3 free content updates that all game owners will receive. Thanks for that!
Difficulty:
The difficulty of the game is a pro and a con at the same time. The beginning was not too easy, some of the levels took me some tries till I was able to master them.
But after I unlocked the second branch of the mortar tower, the mech, this changed instantly. I was able to completed all the following levels very very quickly and also most of them in the first try. I think the mech is simply overpowered.
In contrast, the game offers to change the difficulty, so this issue could be fixed easily, I guess. Still I am satisfied with the difficulty because it took me some time to figure out a good setup for each of the "Heroic" and "Iron" versions.
+ gameplay
+ graphics
+ price w.r.t. content
o difficulty
For me "Kingdom Rush" is now one of the best tower defense series I've every played. "Kingdom Rush Frontiers" is a great sequel; if you liked the first one, you will for sure also like this one. The devs basically did not change much in the already great concept, rather added new levels, enemies and towers.

After a year of being unable to play this game, I finally played it today, and I'm rather disappointed.
Story: 3/10 - The story is very close to non-existent. You play a hardcore criminal named Harkyn who was conscripted to defeat the bad guys and keep them from doing what all bad guys do - dominate or destroy. When the game first starts, you're thrown into the middle of cutscene that has no real solid foundation. Cool visuals, but you have no idea what's going on. Once the cutscene finishes, you build your character (simple decisions of starting equipment and magic spells you want to be able to unlock), and then, without any sort of information or story events leading up to it, you're suddenly in the room of some tower with some scholarly type guy and you're looking for some other guy who is apparently "The Guy."
The story is all over the place, assuming there was a story in the first place.
Gameplay: 4/10 - Basically a spiritual clone of the Dark Souls games (only difference is that you can pause, when all is said and done.) There's talk of fantastic, powerful attack combos, but each weapon only really has one or two attacks, and it's either rapid swining, or slower swinging that doesn't really do much more damage. Nothing comboish about it. The Gauntlet is supposed to be your magical long ranged attacks. Good for doing a chunk of damage to an enemy, but, unless you use a magic energy shard, which you don't ever have many of, you can only shoot the gauntlet maybe once every 30-60 seconds. Utterly useless against bosses. Of course, I wasn't specializing in magic attacks, but I doubt they're much better in a Magic build. You also lose all your experience when you die, and have to run and grab that experience without dying again - because the huge chance that you'll lose all your progress is just so appealing these days. Sure, you can put in all the experience into a checkpoint crystal, but those aren't around every corner like Starbucks. This game is only for the masochist at heart.
Visuals: 6/10 - Not the best looking game, but it does look pretty awesome. Weather effects and environments are pretty cool. Other than that, just about all the environments in most games these days are pretty cool, so LOTF doesn't really bring anything breathtaking to the picture.
In the end, Harkyn's an anti-hero you really have no desire to connect with, the enemies are needlessly tedious to fight, chances are you're not going to find any equipment worthwhile if you go the Light Armor/Deception route (That's basically the rogue build)..... not really a fun mix of crap at all.
Overall: 4/10 - Could've been something. Had a lot of potential, but the devs just made bad design choices and couldn't quite pull off what they managed to put in. Definitely not worth the year wait. Or the $50.

As far as tower defense games go, Kingdom Rush Frontiers is as solid as they come. Adorable, vibrant fantasy graphics and animations, tons of content and replay value, and fantastic sound and music. The tower upgrade paths, the wide variety of heroes to choose from, and the global perk tree made for some wonderful strategic combinations and unique gameplay not normally found in your average tower defense game.
I had a great time experimenting with hero and tower combos. Using the pirate with his ability to call upon the Kraken and having it lock enemies in place while my towers mowed them down was among my favourite combos, and there are countless others to try and discover.
Units are fully voiced in the game, and while it can sometimes get repetitive hearing the same lines over and over, the voice acting was well done and fit the overall cartoon, humerous theme perfectly.
Get those towers up, ready your hero, because at the current price of $10.99 CAD and with more FREE content coming, Kingdom Rush Frontiers is not one you should let slip by.

This game is a sad take on the souls series, the best input it had was the theme and come control changes.
Pros:
1. Some weapon attack combinations were interesting: doing and R1 attack then an R2 attack speeds up the r2 animation.
2. Can cancel healing with other actions.
Cons:
1. rolling, feels sluggish like my character is stuck in a jar of honey even on the lowest weight possible.
2. missing attacks, there are no different attacks for the transitions of movment as seen in the souls series so in essence this game removes many options from combat. R1 with a sword will do a basic swing, running R1 will stop the character on the spot to do the same wing attack instead of an interesting running swing animation.
The only movement transition that leads to an attack is rolling.
3. All bosses have way to much health and the animations can be cheesy taking way to long to finish.
This leads the player to a gameplay of dancing around a boss waiting for its convoluted attack animation to finish just to hit the boss once and doing a small amount of damage.
Bosses should be difficult in ways other then a large health pool and long animations, an example of difficulty without using these methods would be Aava, the King's Pet from Dark Souls 2 DLC.
A boss should not be all about dragging out a fight, its good that the player must take advantage of a small break in the bosses attack but there is so little reqard for exposing a weekness.
If all bosses in the game had half the health and did twice as much damage it could help a lot.
4. My last point will be about the feel of movement in the game, all animations look amazing and blend together perfectly. But there is to much ease in to the beggining of animations, its as if any time i move, roll or jump i need to wait for a wind up for the character to actually start complete those actions.
With a small set of changes for this game i think it really could be something amazing. It looks amazing and sounds amazing but missed the punchline with the formula.

Remember auto-tracking overheads from dark souls? This game is that, minus overheads.
At least, that's what it seems to be, since I can't get past the first boss. The first boss is harder to me than any boss in any game, simply because the game is too fluid. Good games like dark souls shouldn't be fluid. If it is, that means that animations have start up times, and from start up to actual animation is about half a second. That may not seem like a lot, but in the world of reactions, it is. I have the weight for the fastest roll, which, much like dark souls, is a quarter of your maximum, and it still takes forever. Not to mention the fact that the roll takes forever to come out of, and the hit stun is way too long, and a bunch of other technical junk that just doesn't feel right. I got this game because it looked like a good way to satiate the dark souls hunger pangs, but it just reminded me of what I didn't like about some dark souls mechanics.
I'm not completely cynical though, so I will add to this after I've beaten the boss, and depending on what there is, maybe I'll change my recommendation.
UPDATE: Alright, I've beaten the first boss, and I'm now at the second boss. Each boss has a strategy to beating them, no shocker, but much like the rock in the Friday the 13th NES game, whether or not it works all the time is completely up to whatever RNG is deciding whether or not you are worthy enough to progress. And now we get to the interaction scenes. You meet this girl in front of the area for the second boss, and in your first interaction, you tell her whether or not to kill this monk. Alright, good moral decision. Then she tells you about a lost family heirloom, and all the answers are "be a♥♥♥♥♥♥" Then, when you go to end the conversation, you say "I don't care." Not the morally ambiguous "I must go now" or some♥♥♥♥♥♥like that. You instead say "Tata for now ♥♥♥♥er." I'll probably play more though, because I have a problem.
UPDATE 2: Admiteddly, I didn't play a lot of this game when I first said I don't recommend it, however now that I've beaten the second boss I can say that this game is alright. It's not great, but it's not attrocious. The rating it has on the store page is what I'd say is perfect. I have mixed feelings for it, where part of me just says this game is not fun, but another part (my DS mind) says I could play this a lot longer.
P.S. The hit stun is affected by poise, but I'm not sure how much, because I haven't tooled around with it.

First of all, if you think that this game is like your traditional point n click game (like Nancy Drew) then this game is not the game your looking for because Telltale Series game are a bit more than just point n click, You control the actions, relationships and dialogoues of the characters in the story.
The Walking Dead is a Telltale Game Series where your decisions affect the flow of the story and not the actual ending itself. You decide what dialogues you see fit for the situation and the actions you choose affects your relationship towards the other characters.
If you want to embody your own personality into the protagonist (Lee Everett) then go for it. You might even know what it feels like to make tough decisions and what it feels to make big sacrifices. This game is not just choosing dialogues but also interacting with the environment. (but not like Nancy Drew)
The story is totally very good. It would make you feel like your watching the series itself. The ending is very sad and touching. It can make you shed tears.
This game is really worth buying but I recommend that you buy it when it's on sale (preferrably a daily deal) so that you'll be able to buy the DLC and Season 2 for a cheaper price.
The 400 Days DLC is not worth its price since it's quite very short for the 5 additional characters but what's good about it is that the actions you chose on Season 1 and 400 days will be carried over to Season 2. That's why it's worth buying Season 1, 400 Days and Season 2 altogether. Overall, it's a great game with a totally touching story. By the way, I'm not a fan of the series but I highly recommend it to everyone.

I would highly recommend you stay away from Fallout 4 for a 4 main reasons.
1. The entire game is focused on gunplay and will very rarely have any quests with choice or diplomacy involved. It's also oversaturated with copy and paste quests with objectives that boil down to "kill x amount of enemies" or "retrieve x by doing a dungeon". Combat encounters are also not interesting because there are only a handful of enemy types and 90% of them just shoot you, which means the only thing that separates a radier from a super mutant is how much you have to shoot them. The gunplay may be better than it's predecessors but it's not enough to hold up an entire game.
2. The writing and quests are incredibly bland. Even though the game has "4 endings" it only truly has 2 ending states. 1 is blowing up the evil scientists and 2 is siding with the evil scientists. If you're a long time fallout fan you should know that in just about every fallout game previous you would get a complex ending depending on what actions you did in many parts of the game. You only get rewarded with one prerendered cutscene which is basically the protagonist talking about everything you already know, things completely unrelated, and saying that "war never changes" in the end. I should also mention that you have a voiced protagonist, less dialouge options (yes, yes, explain, and sarcastic yes). You also have no skills, tag skills, traits, or even skill checks, which takes the RP out of RPG.
3. No character buliding. Since they've done away with stats and the like all the rpg elements are resigned to your special stats and the "perks" that go along with them. Perks do not function as they have in any other fallout game because they not serve the purpose of having a leveling system. Every level you get 1 perk point to put into any of the perks you have available. But you'll end up ignoring most of the semi-interesting ones to put it into gunplay or modding your weapons, because almost all of the quests invole shooting people. The way they make you upgrade your weapons skills is also very annoying. Your weapon upgrades are not based around making weapons types better (guns, energy weapons, melee, unarmed) but having the upgrades only effect certain weapon firing types (auto, semi-auto, etc) which sucks any variety the gunplay still could have had. That means if you found a really cool gun you can only viably use it if it fires the way that corresponds with what you put your perk points into. It's confusing for new players, and annoying for all players.
4. Bloatware and Paid Mods. For those unaware bloatware is a type of software that takes up a large amount of hard drive space. And with the new paid mods it earns that title. Because their new paid mod initiative (that is patched into every game now) installs all of the mods that are available to purchase, your harddrive is going to be full with useless data. Not to mention that paid mods are one of the scummiest things to come out in a long time. I don't think bethesda understands that mods are made out of love for a game, not to bleed consumers dry. Even if you're ok with everything above I wouldn't buy this game because you'd be supporting this terrible buisness practice.
I would not recommend anybody play this game. With the 60 dollars this game costs you could buy every other game in the fallout series. If you're more of a fan of shooter games buy the new DOOM, it's miles better than this and you can even make your own levels with their snapmap mode. And if you want to play the settlement mode (that isn't even worth mentioning) just ♥♥♥♥ing buy Minecraft, it's a fraction of the cost and updates are free. Go buy yourself a nice dinner or 10 of everything mcdonalds value menu, because you'll get more enjoyment out of that than playing Fallout 4.
TL;DR: Gameplay is boring, writing is bland, it has paid mods, it's bloatware, go buy something else.

Do not let my playtime fool you, I have spent hundreds of hours offline playing this game. Also, this review is mostly to do with 1.0 and development, because the Stable branch was last updated half a year ago and version 1.0 is the closest thing to the final product.
TL;DR: The game has had a patchy history, but it has paid off in the end. Version 1.0 is great, but if you're interested in it: buy the game NOW before it is released, because it is very likely the price will be raised with the release of version 1.0
Now, where do I start with this game...
I have owned starbound for about 2 years now, and it's had some massive changes done to it. Starbound used to be this awesome space survival adventure sandbox rpg game with massive potential. The community was very supportive and the game had a clear direction it was going in. The same can be said about the game in its current state, but something happened along the way. I don't know what the exact cause was, but the whole scheme changed, drastically.
Long story short, the game has went through a few phases of rapid updates with nothing in between. Along the way the community had a falling out over a massive change in genre and development process. Another thing I've heard of was the developers censoring discussion and banning people who wanted refunds and/or heavily criticized the game, but I have no idea whether these are true or not. Anyways, the game went from survival space adventure rpg to uber-casual Teraria with fetch quests. This is about to change with version 1.0
I can't remember how, but I secured a version of Enraged Koala (the version from 2014) back in 2015, and recently I've modded the **** out of it. It's AMAZING! So amazing that I've spent dozens of hours playing it. But as I played, I couldn't help but wonder how the game was doing. I then discovered the sheer beauty of the Nightly branch. For those who don't know, a messy Starbound 1.0 is available for play in Nightly, and I absolutely love it. I love it so much that I've installed the mod that fixes it (link at the end for those who want it) and moved it out of my steam folder so I can play it without worry of game-breaking updates. I have to say, I'm impressed with how far this game has come. I thought this game was done for back in Q1 2015, but I'm glad I was wrong.
Version 1.0 brings back the survival and adds a lot to all aspects of the game. It gives you a reason to prep for planets, to save up money, and to build yourself a place to live on a planet. Quests vary from bosses to protection missions, and all of them give you a worthwhile reward. The Outpost develops as you progress through the game, and so do your crafting stations. There are a variety of crafting stations in the game that all require each other to make things. Crafting recipes are realistic, but not too hard to make. For example, fences not only require wood, but string to hold them together. Armor requires you to get more than just the iron/tungsten/etc. to make them, you also need the leather or fabric for padding. Something new to 1.0 is the variety of gameplay styles. You can be a pirate who sells valuable treasures from temples, or a farmer who lives off the land and makes a living selling crops, or an adventurer completing quests for alien races on different planets. You could be a combination of all three, the choice is yours to make.
With all of this in mind, there is a central story that is optional to progress through, but expands the outpost. No spoilers: You start at your Protectorate graduation ceramony on earth, but it is quickly halted and you are forced to flee to escape danger. You meet a woman who will help you defeat this danger, but you must aquire 6 "keys" in order to stop it, each from a different race. In order to find these keys, you must learn about the culture and history of each race in order to uncover their locations.
I will change my review entirely once version 1.0 comes to the stable branch. I will be playing through the whole thing and giving a complete review of the game. I heavily recommend buying the game now! Odds are Chucklefish will raise the price of the game once it leaves Early Access. I give the messy version of Starbound 1.0 an 8/10.

Steer clear of this.
I've spent nearly 1000 hours modding and testing, never once finished the game.
This is a typical sandbox shooter that just happens to be in the Fallout setting.
It's an alternate 50's timeline where the world has been devastated by nuclear war.
Still, it's more technologically advanced than today with handheld lasers and nuclear fusion in your pocket.
For once, they've taken hints from the modding community and included crafting of weapons and settlements.
But you need DLCs to really take advantage of this. So consider that thoroughly.
You will spend the entirety of the game lugging around trash you need to build weapon/armor modification and building "blocks".
If you're a packrat, then you will also spend most of this time encumbered. Slowly walking wherever you go.
You are given the title of General of the Minutemen, if you so choose.
Being a general does not mean you command anything.
Other factions also gives you fancy titles, but in the end...
You are told what to do and go do it as a lackey for some no-name idiot, and to adopt the ideology of the faction you represent.
In the end, not a single npc recognizes your efforts, so it's a thankless task you do because killing stuff gives experience.
It's a blatant standardized method of leveling. Thin, soulless, mindless.
Indirect methods of solving quests are non-existant.
The main quest of finding your kidnapped son is totally diminished and ends up being something to steer towards once you're done with everything else. This is you being a parent.
But hey. You get'a shoot stuff, so no need think.
As a wasteland sandbox shooter with the Fallout feel, it's ok. But it doesn't have the essence of Fallout.
It's a brainless shooter directed at the console generation with little depth and attention to story.
You're pretty much forced to join a faction if you really want something out of this, and then be told what to do.
So you get to be a glorified janitor to clean up the wasteland and fix lodgings for mindless idiots that has been living in the wasteland their entire lives, yet cannot defend themselves without your explicit help.
Even when you have a fully defended settlement, settlers still manage to get kidnapped.
And there is only one that could possibly do this daring rescue.
Not the settlers that defend. Not the minutemen. Not anyone but you.
So, in essence, there is no sense to this game.
But then again, it's what we expect from Bethesda. A skeletal game that needs to be fleshed out and bugfixed to be successful.
Hence the creation kit that comes with every Bethesda release, and the plethora of tools and mods following in its wake by the modding community.
Verdict:
By itself, the game is a soulless framework.
It feels bugridden and rushed at every turn, but it's easily overlooked because there's always more to shoot.
It is thanks to the modding tools and the modding community that this game gets a fan base.
And the modding community makes this game great.
This game isn't worth much without DLCs and mods to fix and enrich the game.
I would give it a weak thumbs up if it wasn't for the microtransactions. Thanks a bunch Bethesda.

I've been waiting for this game to come to Steam for a long, long time. It's one of my guilty pleasures, as the game itself isn't very polished. Expect laughably bad voice acting, a kinda dumb story explained in cutscenes, and less-than-tight controls on the bad side. But underneath the thin layer of grime shines one of the most interesting shooters out there. Everything in the game costs the player money (in-game currency, not real). Bullets, armor repairs, grenades, and even saving the game costs. Luckily, you get paid for every kill (more for headshots) and you'll occasionally fight against a "champion" of your choosing (mini-bosses that earn big bucks depending on how fast you kill them). Combat mechanics are pretty cool, if a little unpolished. Each weapon has strengths and weaknesses against particular types of enemies and champions. Some champions have shields that you must figure out how to circumvent, which adds a little strategy to the bigger fights. The world-building in this game is pretty good, too. It definitely nails the whole dystopian war-is-reality-TV theme well. No reason not to try it for the price they're asking here. Check it out!

I'm gonna hop on the review train relatively early.
Bought the first game released for steam and recieved about a week ago a coupon for 25% off on this game. Fairly certain that was the devs that requested that, so you know <3 Ironhide, they respect their fanbase. Even without the coupon, if you've played the first game, you'll love this one.
They've upped the strategy, and made heroes more than just a point and click go here and stand your ground. Control upgrade points as they level up. Heroes keep their levels after battle but it takes a significantly larger amount of time to level them up, levels are unique to each hero. Hero A at level 7? Well, Hero B is at level 3, go grind some earlier levels to level that guy up. Distribute level up points into unique skills for each hero.
Towers have been changed/tweaked, new upgrade paths and gimmicks (the Archery Tower's final upgrades are actually useful now), further you go up certain tower, the more synergy you get with other towers around it, Archery tower for example, has a side path upgrade in one of the level 4 upgrades that effects all towers around it with increase range (has to be a mage, another archery, or bombard tower), also gives chance for criticals to all those towers. Smack an archery tower in the middle of the group and spam the upgrades, watch as your Mages get blown-out-of-the-water range on their attacks.
No new towers though, I'd have hoped for a 5th choice, not just the original four you get in the first game. Oh, new map by the way, and of course it's very pretty.
New Environments, new enemies, same great feel.
My experience this far is that the levels are a lot more close to challenging than they were in the first game, where it was either too easy or too hard. I feel like if I just tweak my strategy in someway with my tower setup/troop positioning/upgrade purchases I'll be successful. A feeling I haven't got with any game since I played Halo: Reach Legendary Difficulty.
8/10, hopefully the next one they step it up a bit more, but definitely a worthy sequel and well worth the money.

A review from a dad on a budget check out my podcast Steam on the Cheap where I review Cheap games on steam and let you know if they are worth your time.
Check out my gameplay video and keep reading below for more.
It is very rare to find a cheap first person shooter on steam so when I saw the $8 price tag on this one I had to try it out.
First off a warning. Even though this game just released on steam (Dec 2014) It was originally released in 2005 so it is a decade old game. I did not realize it at first so good on them to trick me like that. The graphics hold up well and if I were judging this in 2005 I would say it has pretty good graphics.
The gameplay resembles any modern day shooter ie the handling and control layout are almost identical show the lack of innovation over the years. I did not have to look up any keys, they all came naturally except to aim down the sights which is the middle mouse button and can not be remapped.
There are  parts of this game that I am really enjoying. The first part deals with the name of the game, Bet on Soldier. At the beginning of a level you can pick a few named bad guys and wager cash on whether or not you will kill them in a 1 on 1 match. Stronger baddies award more money of course. The plays out like an early nemesis system in Middle Earth. When you come across a named guy it zooms in , there is some chatter between the two of you and then you fight. None of your followers or other bad guys on the map at the time can join it so its mano y mano. You win you get the cash, you lose you start from your last save point. There is a time limit on the match and if you run out of time you lose. This separated the game from other shooters and is a big reason that I am going to recommend this game.
The second part I am enjoying is the story. It is very indepth and pretty good too. Some of the old style cut scenes are painfully long due to slow moving people but it does not take away from the story you are being told. The creators did a good job with it.
Lastly this game is hard on the higher difficulty settings. On easy you will probably die a few times but mostly you can run and gun. On hard you really need to put thought into your loadout, companions and in game strategy or you will be respawning often
If you are looking for a cheap FPS to occupy your time I would definitely suggest this one. THe levels are long and really challenging on higher difficulties. Even though I have yet to beat it I have put 3 hours into it and think it is a game that will last well over 8 hours putting it at that dollar an hour range I like for budget games.
If you found my review helpful let me know by clicking yes at the bottom. Until next time cheers

Bet on Soldier is a European-made, non-triple-A First Person Shooter from the mid-00's, the era of Doom 3, Unreal 2, Far Cry 1, F.E.A.R. 1, Killzone 1, etc. It plays mostly like a typical FPS from that period.
Combat is more arcade-like than in modern war FPS; enemies dodge and strafe quite a lot, and if they're wearing body armor it takes several bullet hits to break their armor before you can kill them. Levels can be quite large, with many open outdoor areas, although moving through levels is a fairly linear path. There is no aiming down iron sights; aiming your weapon simply causes your view to zoom in.
Voice acting and cutscenes are fairly typical of most European, non-triple-A games... in other words, pretty much MST3000 quality. Though the gameplay is solid and the graphics are actually pretty good for the time period (comparable to games like Unreal 2, Doom 3, or Butcher Bay). While production values are lower than a triple-A title, they are decent and MUCH higher than something like Chernobyl Commando or Alpha Black Zero.
The game's main distinguishing feature is that everything revolves around money. Instead of picking up health and bullets from enemies, you earn money from killing them and spend it at reload stations to refill your ammo and armor. Not having to worry about picking up items means you can focus entirely on the combat; the flip side is that if you're wasteful with your bullets or armor, you can run out of money and be unable to proceed further.
The game is harder than average, but not as difficult as the hardest FPS games from that period. It is, for example, a lot less frustrating than Iron Storm was.
The Steam version seems to run perfectly fine on modern systems, and has even been updated to support 1080p resolution (up to 1920x1080) natively, without needing to mess around with the cfg files. This was a pleasant surprise. I am playing on Windows 7 64 bit and have not experienced any bugs or crashes after 3 missions.
Multiplayer uses the defunct Gamespy Arcade and crashes instantly for me, so I wouldn't count on it.
I would recommend it if you've played it back in the day and want to play it again, or if you enjoy mid-00 shooters and have some experience with European-developed FPS titles (i.e. Chrome, Chaser, Iron Storm, Alpha Prime, Boiling Point/Xenus, Exodus from the Earth, Ubersoldier, etc.)and thus can go in knowing there will be some rough edges to expect.

Summary: "And here I thought Dark Souls 2 was slow, but here we have the aptly nicknamed: Clunky Souls."
Definitely would recommend a controller; the lack of camera centering button could easily have been incorporated like with Dark Souls' lock-on style: press to lock-on if enemy is present or centre camera if there aren't. Moreover, movement would be easier as the enemies seem to have a huge attack hit-box that can swing at almost 360 degrees.
I was drawn into this game due to the combat style where, like Dark Souls, it was a little more than mere button mashing to knock out your opponent (see Skyrim).  And coming from Vaatividya's video I saw it could be an enjoyable game. However, I found this game to be quite unplayable.
One major flaw when I first played this game was that it eats up so much memory and froze often. Annoyance is an understatement as I had cleared the first boss and a bit of the area thereafter, but had to restart the game only to find all my progress had been lost. Subsequent attempts at beating the boss again reinforces the name: "Clunky Souls" where I found fighting the game mechanics more so than the actual enemies.
But speaking of enemies, the ones with the greatshield are the worst, including the bosses. Their numerous attacks leave you with little stamina after dodging to get behind them and get even a single hit in. They hit hard, have ridiculous defence and are difficult to punish. Of course, baiting the right attack to land the backstab is possible, but it's very tedious just going round in circles.
My lack of gameplay time has been due to frustration with the game's performance and unresponsive combat. While it's flattering for it to be compared to Dark Souls, in my opinion, it's just more of a comparison of how Dark Souls does it much better. I really wanted to like this game because I wanted the sophisticated combat, but unfortunately it fails to give me another Dark Souls experience.
EDIT no. 3: my opinion on this game keeps changing. While it can be enjoyable to an extent of exploration and combat, the enemy designs are terrible. For one thing, once they hit you, it's nigh on impossible to avoid their follow-up combo, draining both health and stamina if you were blocking, already making counter-attacks unlikely. And the second is that so far there are only a few enemy types in the game. They are introduced gradually but from what I've seen there are only about six basic types whose health and damage spike without warning.
Never have I played a more relaxing video game. Beware if you start this game you may just start having a desire to buy a farm.

[Review for the February 2016 Update]
TLDR?; Great game, however recent update has changed the entirety of it. Replaced required currency with items that must be collected in mass to even be of use, bosses are harder, weapons are weaker, was time consuming before-hand and is now even more so due to this update.
Let me start off by saying this game is... or was... great. It was utterly amazing, the simplicity was addicting and the gameplay was phenomonal for a stand-alone pixelated 3D MMO, especially for an E-rating. You jump in with an assortment of classes, rank up and get better equipment, meet challenging bosses and see astonishing maps and detailing with the best ranking system I've seen yet, leveling can either be an easy or difficult accomplishment and the best part about it is that you can play this came solo and still find enjoyment no matter what.
Now let's touch the dirty parts of this. Before the update there was an easily obtainable form of currency by Mastery Rank 10 called Flux, this Flux is required in mass numbers to do a number of things such as creating equipment, trading with other players, and even creating neccessary items. There was the harder obtainable Dragon Coins, which were used to purchase Dragon Souls, which upon consumption would give you a Dragon Level. Five would be a pet, ten would be a mount, then the mount would level up as you reach higher levels until you reached a full-fledged dragon that could fly, and give you massive stat boosts. The update switched this. Now, the oh-so require Flux can only be acquired through completing 45 dungeons in twenty to fifteen minutes, which this objective is seen after reaching Master Rank 10. Sounds easy, right? Negative, ghost rider. In order to accomplish this, you must be part of the two bonus classes in the objective. The bonus classes are essentially randomly generated, and they grant a certain class the ability to complete a dungeon and get it counted for three. With out this, you are racing between several worlds for fifteen to twenty minutes, killing several bosses (which can be difficult dependant on your area), all the while trying to even get to them from across the other side of the map. Not only this but you also must beat other players to get there, which some of the more experienced have insane speed boosts due to other mounts, and pay-to-play players have a large boost from this. Some might question, "Is this enough to give a bad review, though?" Maybe. However there is more. In the recent update, high leveled items were buffed. Now you may be wondering, "Doesn't that contradict your statement that other players have advantages?" No. This is only for weapons, which do not give you speed buffs. This comes with the problem that the bosses were not buffed, they remain the same difficulty. Completing a Shadow Tower is now even harder than it was, and for those who have not played the game, a Shadow Tower is essentially what you would call an "end-game level". This is for high ranking players, with very powerful weapons. Even with those powerful weapons you must work together. Before the buffing, the bosses were extremely difficult and took several tries to complete, however now it takes a lot more. There's still more to come, however.
