TLDR: Overall, moments of entertainment locked behind odd design choices and unresolved glitches that makes it impossible to recommend.
EDIT: And I feel bad for not being able to recommend it because I did have some good fun and effort was clearly made.
First the good:
-The character/monster/environment designs are well done, it's all massive muscles, massive armour and massive weapons but if you don't mind that it's nicely done.
-When the combat works, it can be fun.
The mixed (subjective):
-The armour sets are well designed, as mentioned above, but the standard as you go through set progression is inconsistent. For light armour for example, you get the best designed armour about half way through then get sets that seem much more 'vanilla' or are (I believe) reskins of previous sets.
-The story isn't terrible, but I'm still unsure about the premise. Why exactly is Adyr the god considered a 'villain'? I may have missed an audio log that explains this, but then it is still missable.
-There is a universal cooldown on spells, use one and they all go on cd (at least the ones from the same school do, can't verify whether it applies to other schools). On some combinations this may make sense, on others it seems overly restrictive. Keep in mind that without massive xp investment into faith (magic), the mana cost of each spell is likely prohibitive of chain casting anyway. Not impossible mind you, but when you factor in the cast time of each spell and the likelihood of interruption by enemy hits, a gcd seems superfluous.
-Combat staggering seemed unpredictable across the board, both on you and the enemies. There seemed no way of knowing ahead of time whether Harkyn would get staggered by any given enemy's attacks or whether they would be staggered by his.
-Certain classes may seem underpowered, mileage may vary. Rogue class definitely could have used some life steal baked in to a spell.
-Majority of voice work is bland, not all but a lot of it.
-The rune/crafting system seemed inconsistent. The game features a system where you can invest xp into locked runes  to increase the likelihood of better quality buffs but the return on this seemed very disappointing. Possibly rectified with better 'Luck' character stats but that's uncertain.
The bad:
-The hit detection is suspect. Weapon strikes simply may decide not to land, spell hits may just not register.
-Enemy projectiles may not hit you when they should and may seek you out through walls.
-Equipment stats are confusing. You are given numbers without context. Conversely some items have only 'fluff' descriptions.
-The camera may decide to snap to a completely obscured perspective during 'backstabs'.
-Spell effects may also overwhelm your vision.
-The gauntlet is intrusive and frequently redundant. It seemed underpowered no matter which class or loadout was used, an enemy could always be reached to melee them anyway, using it costs mana that would 9 times out of 10 be better used on spell casting and it is unalterably bound to the stance swapping button which gets in the way during combat.
-The physics are unbelievable in a bad way. Enemies may do a U-turn mid leap, defying momentum. The enemy also has a bad habit of tracking your motion during weapon swings that would likely snap their bones, also rendering combat maneuvering futile. This becomes more of a problem with the more fragile classes.
-Pathing is incompetent. Enemies may get stuck on corners or non existent obstacles, may reset and speed off to their original point (no, not that one demon dog who is scripted to do something similar).
-Harkyn's magic is wildly unreliable. Magic may simply not do what it is supposed to. Direct damage spells may just not land despite hitting the mark. Buffs may drop off before their proper duration or not do as described. Bad pathing also applies here.
-Even after hours of play time, the cumbersome nature of the spell casting can still be infuriating. Enemy AI is unreliable as to attacking during casting, they may knock you out of it or stand there and wait. A hit the wrong side of a millisecond may interrupt a 'complete' cast.
-Controls are unreliable, Harkyn may simply ignore commands. The most frequent suspect for me was the running shield bash attack, it simply didn't happen about 40% of the time and would land Harkyn in hot water each time. Dodges may simply not occur either.
-Saves may not be complete, by which I mean you can save your progress at a checkpoint or even move to a new area and quit and when you reload, the game may simply not have saved to that point. On a whim.
-Desktop crashes. Frequent and exacerbated by the above problem.

Full disclosure; I have done several things to make the game as easy on me as possible. Many of the ingame options includes disabling certain features, including debuff chances and monster corpses (Which can mess with your attack formations) to name a couple. Alongside that, I’ve utilized the workshop and downloaded several quality-of-life mods that include bigger inventory (and thus higher payouts at the end of quests, if you nab enough things), Stronger Start (which effectively buffs your starter two heroes), and level restriction removal which allows me to bring higher level people on lower level missions which would help “Carry” new characters. There’s several more but nothing quite so severe as what I have done to XCOM2. If you people only knew...
You’ve probably already heard about Darkest Dungeon. It’s one of the very few Early Access success stories. What we have here is a roguelike turned based roleplaying game. For those just joining us, “Rogue” was an older game, effectively inventing its own genre of difficulty and progression. Roguelikes tend to be punishing, destroying your early game while slowly earning currencies and upgrades that continually aid you in your further attempts.
In the story, some nobleman got some gold fever and started digging around his lands and unleashed a literal eldritch abomination which cast a swath of land into darkness, turning the whole place into a hellscape. I don’t know what matter of character we, as the player, plays as but we lead a band of mercenaries across these lands to explore dungeons and forests. You scrape up gold and treasure, eventually upgrading your township and champions so you can take on higher challenges. The overarching goal is to assault the Darkest Dungeon itself, which I’m sure is full of good times and parties.
That’s the baseline concept but there are a ton of nuances that go into the game. I for one am happy to have some turn based combat in my life again, the last memory of which was Final Fantasy X which I enjoyed greatly in my teenage years. There may be a reason the genre faded in the background as it’s a bit of a flow-breaker, which had no place in a world of Call of Duty’s and Halo’s and Arkham’s. Darkest Dungeon makes the concept really work, with an interesting art style that makes it look like you’re reading an ancient tome with plenty of pictures to go along with the legend, helped by the narrator who occasionally spouts antiquated language like “Perched at the very precipice of oblivion...” You really do feel like you’re playing through an interactive book at times.
If you’ve played a Dark Souls or any roguelike game, you probably know the score. Your people will die. If they don’t die, they might get to a point where you can no longer tenably sustain their negative quirks and high stress levels. Quirks and stress (stress being comparable to any insanity mechanic in a Call of Cthulhu RPG or Amnesia game) bring your heroes down constantly, from easily ignored to debilitating. I don’t care if my tank has -3 speed, but I do care when someone gets a tapeworm which doubles their food consumption. That’s basically♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥my money away. At a certain point, characters become so stressed, they gain an affliction which is usually much harsher. A healer of mine once became “Paranoid”, not only fleeing to the back of the group but sometimes wrestled control away from me on her turn, using her own decision making to pop a heal or attack without my command. These can be cured for high sums of gold in your township but most players choose to abandon the character.
Thankfully, retreating is a possible option. You don’t get the high payout quest rewards but you do keep everything you acquired in the dungeon itself. If you made it past 80% of the dungeon but all your people are at 10% health, one of them is bleeding, one of them is paranoid, it might just be better to flee, take your earnings, and send some of the worse-off characters on their way. I’ve probably abandoned quests more often than I’ve completed them, but I’m still making some progress in the game and that’s what matters.
Now, I’m a fairly casual scrub player. I like my games fun and easy if at all possible but there is something positively enchanting about Darkest Dungeon. The combat is incredibly intense, and I can feel my heart skip a beat every time I see “dodge” or “miss” pop up. Every time my people don’t land a blow, it opens me up for another attack and that frightens me to a decent degree. The game’s tone is dreadful but it works in its favor with its highly stylized... style. I just like looking at the game, which is impressive because I find myself thinking about it when not playing it. Due to the steam summer sale, I also was able to get Watch Dogs 2, but this game is drawing more of my attention than any triple A game at the moment and that’s always a good sign.
If I had a complaint, it’s probably the same complaint you might have seen while skimming over other reviews. The random number generator aspect of the game can be seen as a detriment. People like to progress, and we also like having our decisions matter in the grand scheme of things. Other times, it feels hopeless. I once equipped a character with a -25% stress trinket only to have a very harsh fight with a Madman enemy constantly unload high stress on the entire team before I was able to take him out. It’s moments like that, that give me the sense of “Why did I even bother?”
I do believe that’s how some of this is supposed to work. Retreating from dungeons more often than completing them makes it all the more satisfying when I am actually able to complete one and see that sweet, juicy 4500 gold enter my theoretical bank account.
Still, there can be a bit of that old “nothing I do matters” feeling that creeps up while you play. I certainly get that from time to time but I’m doing my best with some of the easiest settings cranked up and I find myself enjoying the experience anyway.
Would I recommend this game? As usual it depends on what you look for in games. It has plenty to offer for challenge seekers, with a lot of gear management, loot, and town upgrading to cater to any RPG lovers. The general consensus across the internet can be very mixed, with every update having a vocal outcry on things being too easy or too hard. I wasn’t there during many of these updates, I’ve come in two years later into their development and I’m probably experiencing one of the most refined versions of this game and as it is, I’m enjoying it. I’m as surprised as anyone.

You are the owner of the hamlet with an obsessive need to find its secrets. The people who come to raid are either greedy, or adventurous, or evil, or looking for redemption, or for some other kind of personal gain. You do not care about them, only about your hamlet. Send a team to the dungeons without any torches or provisions. Let them go crazy or get injured as long as they bring back treasure to rebuild the hamlet. If they become too damaged, you dismiss them and find another sucker to take his/her place. This is how you play this game. It is about the hamlet, not about the adventurers.
If people are looking for a highly stress inducing, teeth grinding, scream filled gaming experience in a simple 2D game, then Darkest Dungeon is the game for you. I have never come across a game in my entire life that solely depended on RNG. In a way, I consider this a tiny Dark Souls like game, except you can't control everything in the Dark Souls games, such as dodging, landing hits, and encountering/avoiding enemies. This is by far one of the most challenging and yet highly satisfactional experience I have ever had playing Darkest Dungeon, if you have the fortitude/patience to outlast your own stress.
Honestly the negatives depend and vary from player to player. If i was to point out something i disliked that would be the lack of inventory space on long quests. Also this game is sometimes dependent on luck i have lost heroes in the most unfair scenarios possible. In addition, the boss battles are abosolute hell. They are not a walk at the park it will take a few deaths to know how to win them.

This game will truly test your stress control and patience. A careful, methodical player who takes time to set up each run and adapt to new situations as best he/she can will prosper, though everyone will eventually be confronted with the fact that heroes, even if well-managed, are ultimately only human.
I would definitely recommend skimming through a couple videos seeing how people prepare for different areas, and how well it goes. You can find detailed spreadsheets giving outlines for what to bring where. Youtuber Baertaffy has played this game so much, and at the start of his videos he explains who and what he's bringing where and why. Maybe watch the first few minutes of a handful of his DD videos to get an idea of how to prepare. If you're unsure on what to bring, overpreparation is a safe bet. Bring lots of food and shovels.

Sometimes you get some different contracts that are like a sub contract to your main contract which has a different set of conditions. Completing these will net you extra money most times and sometimes something a little different, like an item.
What units you use can determine your success or failure, keeping a healthy mix as much as possible is the key to your success. Different types of units have different strengths and weaknesses, the game teaches you the basics in this regard and as far as I remember doesn't expand into the special units. So there's some experimentation there on your part when you eventually encounter these units.

Metal Slug X is a "Remixed" and updated version of Metal Slug 2, with some news compared to the First chapter.
Metal Slug X is a side scrolling shooter, and like its predecessor it presents the same base elements: a ridiculous amount of enemies, prisoners of war to free as bonus, hidden elements and enormous Boss Machines.
Does it have something new? Of Course! First of all you can choose between 4 characters (totally ininfluent, but it's nice to see the two guys from the First Metal Slug and two new girls), there are lots of new mass destruction weapons while the old ones have been improved, there are new kind of enemies, new status as the "mummy" (there are mummies that can turn you into a mummy as well just with their purple breath) and "Biiiig!" (when you pick up too much food you become fat and your weapons become more powerful, though you become too slow). More important news are the vehicles: a more powerful metal slug, a mecha, a plane and a camel.
However  the most important news is the difficulty. Metal slugs are always crowded, but X is a total Mayhem, really overcrowded. It's pretty difficult not to die even at the easiest difficulty level, so this chapter is a very hard challenge.
Of course, as usual, you can play Coop with a friend on the same computer or through Network.

Metal Slug X was initially released in March of 1999, and it is a revised version of Metal Slug 2; both games feature the same characters, storyline, and missions. This version includes increased difficulty, as well as solutions to some technical issues that were unresolvable at the time in Metal Slug 2. Initially an arcade-only release, Metal Slug X has found itself ported to various platforms throughout the years, and it finally found its way to Steam in late 2014.
The Metal Slug franchise is a must play for any fan of run and gun arcade games, the titles are cult classics that never gained the popularity that they've deserved throughout the years. Metal Slug X takes place two years after the events of the original game, and the player can choose between a variety of four characters; Marco, Tarma, Eri, and Fio. The former two characters returned from the original entry, while the latter two were new additions to the series at the initial time of release. You will face off against an onslaught of Rebel Force opponents, an army with a brand distinctly ripped off from the Nazi logo, while also taking on various other enemies such as mummies and aliens.
Believe it or not, Metal Slug actually has a fairly well thought out storyline, and while there is no in-game dialogue that progresses this feature, it is up to the player to interpret the majority of what is happening by being aware of what is going on within each mission. The real chunk of the story can be found on the official Metal Slug website, while back in the day you'd have to hunt down a copy for the home NeoGeo that was complete with a booklet. The game itself is rather short, coming in with 6 missions in total that last for just a few minutes each; although the ending boss battle takes up a large amount of time. It's important to remember that this game was a huge quarter grab back in the day, with its high difficulty and one-hit player death, so the lack of longevity to the game can be forgiven in this day and age.
The graphics are classic and timeless 2D pixel artwork. Everything from the backgrounds, to the explosions, to the enemies and character models are deliciously detailed. Every mission is radically different from its predecessor, although there is little variety in enemies. Not to mention the brilliant soundtrack, which has everything from upbeat, frenzied tracks to laid back, jazz inspired scores. The game has definitely aged well, and I would hate to ever see one remastered in 2.5D. Many people complain that this title has "slow downs", and while this is true, the actual in-game FPS counter never drops below 60. It's the same scenario as the Mega Man Legacy Collection, in that it's just how the game was at the time it originally released, and as such it has not been modified in order to give it that true retro feeling.
If you're unfamiliar with the Metal Slug franchise, here is a brief breakdown of what sets it apart from other arcade/run and gun games: While not largely based around it, the game does have a point system where you can show off your highscores; there are P.O.W.s that you can save who grant items to increase your points, and every shot that you land on an enemy also increase your score. If you die and have to use a continue, your score is reset, as well as the amount of P.O.W.s that you've saved. There are various weapons that you can gather, and all but the pistol have a limited supply of ammo; while your favorite gun will depend on your play style, you can choose from ones such as the laser, heavy machine gun, rocket launcher, flamethrower, drop shots, and much more.
While I do not necessarily consider Metal Slug X as much of a fan-favorite or classic in comparison to the first or third entries, it's still a great installment into this timeless series. If you've never played a Metal Slug game before, I suggest picking up 3 instead of this one, however, simply because it's better and more fun (in my opinion, of course). The Steam version of Metal Slug X includes the original Arcade Mode, where you must go from Mission 1 through Mission 6 in one sitting, lest you lose your progress, and also a Mission Mode, where you can quit once you get to the next mission and then pick up on the one that you left off at. The game also features leaderboards, and a variety of difficulties ranging from easy to very hard. For those of you with friends, there is a two-player mode as well that is suitable for both local and online play. If you're a hardcore fan, pick it up for full price; if you're skeptical of your enjoyment, wait for a sale.

I'm really glad this game saw a PC release. Metal Gear Rising (developed by the same team, Platinum Games) was my first real venture into the ultra fast-paced side of the hack n' slash genre, and Bayonetta feels similar in all the right ways. Action-packed, challenging, and charming, Bayonetta is probably a worth addition to your library if you're a fan of difficult, action-oriented games.
There's no stealth mechanics or lenghty puzzle sections here. From start to finish, Bayonetta is always ready to throw enemies at you, sometimes when you least expect it. Bayonetta is mostly a hack n' slash title in the same vein as games like Metal Gear Rising, Devil May Cry, God of War, and so on. By default, Bayonetta's real only defensive option is to dodge (dodging at the last second will activate a slow motion mechanic) and as such its one of those games where the best defense is a strong offense; you just gotta kill enemies before they kill you, plain and simple. Coming from somebody that's beaten MGR on Revengeance difficulty, Bayonetta is a hard game. But definitely in a good way.
A good story means nothing if it happens to characters you don't care about. Most of the game's supporting characters have their own distinct personality, and although they seem shallow and one-dimensional at times they'll largely grow on you by the end. The best character is easily Bayonetta herself. I went into this game expecting her to just be blatant eye candy with a generic dominatrix-type personality (which is how it starts, admittedly) but over the course of the game we see that Bayonetta cares for the people she's around. She gets mad, she worries, she has a sense of humor, and she's just generally an enjoyable character to follow around. She's far more lovable than she initially seems.
This game is flashy, over the top, self-aware, and for the most part does a pretty good job of knowing what it is and not getting too serious for its own good. Sure, serious♥♥♥♥♥♥goes down as the story progresses, but there's tons of very welcome comic relief all over the place. There's also numerous references to past Sega games, which I'll let you discover for yourself. It's a witty and snarky game, and I think they nailed the tone of it all just right.
No glitches or crashes in my playthrough whatsoever. The framerate was consistently high and there's enough graphical options to make this game look pretty decent, even with it being a console exclusive from 2009.
Bayonetta would have had an amazing storyline if it had been written a little bit better. It mostly makes sense by the end, and all the major plot elements that a story should have are there, but there's a few plot holes that never get entirely wrapped up and some of the story points are a little confusing at first. I also feel like it could've been fleshed out a little more. I wouldn't say the story as a whole is bad, it just had some sloppy execution at some points.
I said earlier that Bayonetta was hard in a good way, and that mostly holds up. However, there are a few frustrating QTE sections that jump at you out of nowhere (some of which may instantly kill you). There's also multiple times where enemies will attack you straight out of a cutscene with absolutely no warning, chipping away at your health. This wouldn't be too bad if Bayonetta wasn't a score-focused game, but it is. If you're playing for points, Bayonetta will very heavily punish your score if you die or use items to heal yourself or make yourself stronger. It's never fun with a game penalizes you so heavily for dying and then kills you in a quick, cheap way.
No matter how many times you ask.
Bayonetta's main downfalls are a story with somewhat weak writing and a couple of cheap, unforgiving gameplay sections. Beyond that, it's a fun and standard hack n' shash title with lots of spectacular over-the-top goodness and genuinely fun moments. It's a little on the short side, but that doesn't matter since there's NG+ and a decent amount of incentive for multiple playthroughs. Pick it up if you have the money.

Although my usual preference is for straight strategy games,  this title emphasizes strategic awareness and teamwork over reaction time making it a more thoughtful experience than your usual online carnage festival. After a break i had - in wich a wipe took place - i returned to Fractured Space and saw again why i like this game.
It is basically a MOBA with capital (space) ships from the third pespective. You got your to expected weapons, utilities and drones to fight against other ships. There are currently three factions with a (yet sparse, some would say) tech tree with different ships to research. The main types also apply in Fractured Space: Offense, Defence and Support with according abilities. (May call them Damage Dealer, Tank and Healer). And even with the currently little pool of ships there are some interesting ways to combine your forces. Also you can form a crew, as you choose five crewmembers out of a bunch with different specifications and thus granting you some bonuses for the ship you can match with your playstyle (sadly there are quite few crewmembers at the time)
What i like about FS is the graphic and the design. The three factions have all interesting shipdesigns and i simply adore the modular construction of these giant spaceships. Also the sound is very pleasing. Ignore the fact of soundless space - the lasers ingame are awesome.
Of course you must keep in mind that Fractured Space is a Early Access game and so in state of developement.
There is only one map and gamemode aviable right now and you only can invite just one friend to play together.
But i hope there is more to come. Fractured Space has potential and i hope its gonna play it out right and draw the attention of all who like MOBAs, space and/or capital space ships.

This is the first game I've felt strongly enough about to review.
I'm a sci-fi nerd with a power complex and this game gets me. The ship models are breathtaking and feeling the mass of the ship as it resists the changes in velocity is so very very tasty. It's apparent from the start that a lot of love has been put into the game. They even tell you how many crew members are on your ship so that you can quantify your feeling of failure as a commander when your ship is destroyed. While the options are sparse for now, the sheer pleasure of the gameplay is worth well more than the $10 asking fee.I've rarely had such fun in a spce combat sim and I have to say that the variety in Fractured Space keeps me wanting to play and support the developers.
Because damn do they need it. While this is really one of the most well balanced and satisfying space-combat games I've ever come across, there are very large problems with the matchmaking client and server optimization. But the only way that those get fixed is if people play the game. This is a committment I feel good making because what the devs have given us is an absolutely beautiful, immersive, satisfying, and fun(!) experience. Looking at what they've produced for Alpha, I have no doubts that with time and our support they will make this unique and impressive experience even better for their users.

Ruin has come to your game balance. A lot of people (see; Steam reviews and feedback from sites) remember that Darkest Dungeon was better in one of the 2015 Early Access patches, they were in love with the core concept of this game and its difficult, engaging battle system was (at the time) heralded as fair without being a chore to the people.
Red Hook Studios' Chris Bourassa breaks down the creative philosophy of Darkest Dungeon at GDC 2016:
Something went wrong, the final versions of Darkest Dungeon became style over substance.
(Beaten on normal mode, strict ruleset, no mods, without DLC, etc.)
Cool encounters and strategy will forever be destroyed by the game's demand for tedious grind and repeat of stale content over and over. While the grueling, slow pacing of combat is intentional for the feeling of dread that the developers wanted... the reality is that something simple as status effect pop-ups are wasting a large accumulative amount of time before you even get to input a command.
Nothing you do will matter both in narrative and gameplay - at least until you get experienced (as a player, not a statistic.) You will only have a swift time with this game if you're a veteran who has already bored himself with the sheer destitution of content outside of the creative finale dungeons. If you still like the game and yet to beat it, consider the tasks you must perform to get ready for the four final quests.
Fanboys will defend it by saying you have sunk cost fallacy or whatever buzzword at their disposal, just ignore them, there's much better strategy turn based RPGs around. It's safe to say that it gives the most disgusting grind-fests of JRPGs a good name.
Could be fixed, but I doubt they will bother. I hear Radiant mode is just as unfun and people don't love their overleveled guys being underequiped for Champion Dungeons until they mindlessly grind. Ruin has come to your game balance.

I sank hundreds of hours into the original release of Bladestorm on the Xbox 360. When I saw it got an updated release with an added campaign and new features and was available on Steam, I was super excited. Then I got extremely discouraged when I read all of the negative reviews about how poorly optimized it supposedly was. I finally broke down and bought a copy and let me say, the reviews were wrong.
The game runs just as smoothly on my mid-range PC as it did on the console. Yes, it's only on medium settings but it still looks great, especially compared to its appearance on the 360. My husband ended up buying a copy for his computer (a slightly lower end mid-range PC) and it runs beautifully on his computer as well.
We even ran some Co-Op and were really happy with the results. There was some minor issue with synchronization, but everything usually ended up sorting itself out pretty quickly. The end of day scores were wildly inaccurate, but it didn't really matter since we were having fun playing together and chasing down objectives. It also let us experiment with leveling up units that are difficult to level because they tend to start out so weak (knives, archers, fencers, etc.).
There are plenty of other features to poke around in that greatly enhance and improve the gameplay. Bladestorm was already a game that I had fond memories of, now it's gotten even better. My only regret is that I waited so long to purchase it. Definitely looking forward to racking up many more hours of play time.
If you enjoy Dynasty warriors and real time strategy games then you'll probably get some enjoyment out of Bladestorm and I recommend that you purchase it right away.

Bladestorm: Nightmare is a Japanese Warriors-interpretation of the 100 Year War between England and France, featuring a good score of actually existing historical characters. Being a Musou game, it is extremely grindy and only appeals to a niche target audience, but to that audience, it does deliver most superbly. The game is a revamp from the original 2007 console release, scales nicely to 4k and looks pretty good featuring hundreds of units on screen without stutter or any technical issues. The only issues I ever had were random shader flickering every few hours for a scene, apart from that it runs well without crashes or any hiccups.
As for the gameplay itself, you're playing a self-created Mercenary captain called upon by the two clashing forces of the 100 year war and as the game progresses you'll become able to control some, if not all of the key historical characters as part of your 4 squad army. Combat mechanics consists of three special abilities for every unit class and type, which there are roughly three to four dozen of, meaning there's a lot of variety to fiddle around with. The Nightmare campaign which the release is named after features a short fantasy campaign with a fully new roster of monster units which can also be controlled as the game progresses and which can even be partially used in the standard campaign as both campaigns share the same mercenary captain directory (of which in turn you can create several dozens of)
It's fun, tactical, fast paced and horridly grindy.
Short reminder: A gamepad is strongly recommended due to the abysmal keyboard layout (mouse controls are not supported, not even in the game menu)

i was hoping to have this game fill the void of darksouls after a beat the first on xbox and the second on pc, but it falls short on my expectations.
the good:
the graphics are nice, the enemies are interesting and the world seems well designed. you get weapons really quickly and its great to play around and experiment with the different weapons and each one is unique, this might be an erea where it beats the souls games and i hope that darksouls 3 will take a queu here and make their weapons feel more unique.
the bad:
the levels layout is bad, and the game is super linear. i thought DS2 was a more linear experience, but at least there you could chose the other you beat the bosses to a certain degree. here, the game feels supremely railroaded and is more a series of boss fights which aren't really that interesting.
the worse:
the combat feels terrible and doesn't hold a candle to what the souls games offer. the largest issues i had was with the windup to the initial attack and the lockon tracking. i prefer to use heavier weapons, the hallberd is my go to in both Dark souls games, in this game, the windup is to the first strike is so long that even after succesfully dodging, rolling or blocking the enemy attack combo you will still get hit before you can wind up the initial attack. the only way i have found around this is to abuse the sprint heavy attack and even here with the heavy weapons i use having a vertical attack rather than a horizontal one, i tend to miss the enemy  when he strafes. this might be aleviated if you prefer light faster weapons but this is not my prefered play style.
all in all its a decent game, but isn't a good substitute to fill a souls void. buy it on sale maybe, i got it for 20$ on sale and got a few hours of "OK" fun, but its way overpriced and not really worth finishing in my opinion. if i were to give it a score, it would be a 5.5/10. its slightly above average, i haven't run into any bugs or anything, but the game is 100% forgetable.

OMSI 2 is a game where you drive some buses around Berlin. It's very simple, but still fun. Think of it as Euro Truck if it was instead a bus simulator.
Now of course the graphics of the game aren't like a AAA game like Battlefield or anything. But since when are graphics the dictator of how fun a game is? The handling is actually like a heavy bus. Nothing will fly away like a paper airplane or anything like that. The sounds are also beautiful and don't get annoying.
Simply put, OMSI 2 is relaxing, and is just a game to take your mind off of stuff. It's a simple idea, but is still kind of nice.
So why am I giving it a bad rating? Well...
There are some flaws that bother me, such as...
- Finding your way around: At points I pull up to an intersection, and there is 5 arrows around... And I sit there wondering where to go... It's very confusing at points, because some arrows are misleading. I was going stopped at a bus stop when I saw an arrow point left. So I turned left and looked around for another stop... Apparently I was suppose to go forward at that intersection, but nothing said to go forward! They need to add a GPS where you just follow a line.
- Lack of maps and routes: I was so disappointed when I saw only 2 maps... One map has only one route. Berlin has a few more, but they get old really quickly. I want to have some variety please! Want to know where to get more maps?
-DLC: Where do I start... So the game is $35... Care to spend $350? 10x more than the game? No? Then don't buy the DLC... The DLC is severly overpriced since literally all they add is a few more maps and buses. Why would you spend 10x more than a game just to get more out of it? I have checked, the best you're getting out of the sale is around $300... As far as the steam price history website is giving me. I mean, it's ridiculous... I cannot recommend the game because of this.
Save your money. Buy just the game if you want it, spend the extra 300 elsewhere.

Are you an ETS2 or ATS player, but you spent enough time driving trucks? Do you want to have a realistic driving experience without getting your hands dirty? Are you about to get your bus driving license? Then this is the game for you! Sure, it only has a few buses to play with and not more than two maps, but that's no issue! Bus mods are relatively easy to install, but the map mods are hard to install. If you don't want to mess around with the game's files, then you can buy one of the many overpriced DLC, like I did (and I'm regretting it). Anyway, if you do decide that cautious and legal driving is too boring for you, then this game is also for you! Sometimes, buses fly over the city and land wherever they want! And sometimes, the only thing that makes this game mildly entertaining is the fabulous traffic, which is more careful than your grandma when it comes to driving, prompting even the quietest driver to swear at the slow-moving cars!
Graphics aren't the game's selling point, as they are inferior to, let's say, ETS2's graphics. They're fine, but nothing special here.
In the audio department, this game is all right, but the passengers will start talking to you in German, which is a good thing if you even undestand the language. Luckily, I do, and they were comparing me to Michael Schumacher :)
This game is not for the ones that seek fun from simulators, but the fact that it is so close to reality makes up for its problems. Do I recommend it? Sure. Would I pay for the DLCs? Never.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I'd say this game is kind of mediocre. Its gameplay is split up in 2 parts: jump'n'run'n'shoot á la Ratchet and Clank and "investigation mode", which rather plays like a point and click adventure game. It feels more like a console game than a PC game as you not often require the mouse, just while interacting with a scene during investigation mode and in the menus,  furthermore the cutscenes (which seem kind of compressed along with its audio) and the overall graphics seem pretty outdated, considering the game came out in 2008.
But now let's get more into detail:
The combat/jump'n'run sequences is/are okayish. Every weapon is kind of viable, even the weakest one is still usable against the toughest ones, and also every weapon is usable against every weapon, and there isn't much tactics involved. You can dodge bullets, but some parts make it impossible to do so, as some corridors are too narrow to strafe. Fall damage is kind of an odd deal, as you either are fine or die, making you restart from a checkpoint (which feels kind of weird, as it just quickly fades to black and then fades into the last saved position, however sometimes the checkpoints are placed rather inconvenient, since some are around enemies, and while you figure out where you are now after respawning you propably will take a hit or two.
The investigation parts play alot like point'n'click adventure games. You walk around, press spacebar when you are near an interactive scene and take items or use items from your inventory on other items. The first and second one are kind of tough, as the rooms are pretty big, and you don't get much hints on what to do, also items that have no more use doesn't always dissapear from your inventory, making the parts even more tedious to solve with. The third one (and last one) is incredibly easy on the other hand.
Overall the game is, as said, mediocre. It isn't that bad, but also not a masterpiece. The price is kind of justified, considering the quality and the length of the game. However this game is only part 1 of 2 parts, however part 2 will propably never come out as a game (although all remaining cutscenes are on youtube I heard), so it should be kept in mind that this isn't a 'full game' as in a game that has a clear ending. So I reccommend it rather to those who like odd jewels (if you want to call it that) than to those who actually want to buy it and hope to get a good game in the traditional sense.

September 2, 2017
Dear Bethesda Game Studios,
Today I am writing out of concern and disgust on how you have allowed greed drive your decisions that led to the cancer that is the Creation Club. I am a gamer who loves your games specially Fallout 4 and Skyrim. I felt in love with these games in recent years but I want you to know it wasn’t always the case. I actually didn’t like them at all. They were too long and most importantly the grinding was unmanageable for me. It drove me crazy. I bought Original Skyrim a few years back, between broken quests, game breaking bugs and grinding system that was sure to make me insane I decided Skyrim wasn’t for me and uninstalled it from my computer. I always wondered why these games were so popular when they were by recent standards so dated and to me boring. YouTube channels entirely dedicated to both games. If you've played Dark Souls, you know that the game's calling card isn't that it's hard, but it's a very fair game. When you die, it's your fault and you don't feel cheated.
Lords of the Fallen takes the core mechanics of Dark Souls and adds a bit. The graphics are beautiful, the added roleplaying aspect is neat. But at the end of the day, the core mechanics that it stole from Dark Souls are implemented weakly. Hit boxes are awful. I haven't died once where I thought "Okay, that's my fault I got greedy/hasty". The problem is always the mechanics killing you. And that is not a good game.
Lords of the Fallen tries to be a Dark Souls clone and gets everything about it's inspiration horribly, unappologetically wrong. It's difficult for the sake of being difficult so the designers can say "We made a hard game." 4/10, because the graphics are beautiful and that's really the only redeeming quality of the game.
I'll be requesting a refund.

After being very interested in the challenges games like Dark Souls represent I have tried, and failed (many times) to get INTO a Dark Souls game. I tried Dark Souls, Dark Souls II and many other games that use a similar concept such as the direct clone but (whilst at times beautiful) very flawed Lord of the Fallen...and they just never clicked with me. Something about them just seemed off in some way.
Dark Souls 3 is a different beast in my opinion, I have completely and utterly fallen in love with this game.
Visually its stunningly (grotesquely) gorgeous. The art style is captivating. Ive spent quite a bit of the game just bathing in the horrific/gothic architecture. Lighting effects are used to incredible effect on environments and characters or beasties. The first time I encountered a rather large creature (no spoilers) hugging the walls of a huge structure I was in complete awe. Visually its probably one of the best looking games, maybe even the most beautiful game I have ever played. And the creature design is simply awesome. A lot of love and attention has been put into creating every single one of them. Big and small....and HUGE!
Gameplay wise - well, its a Dark Souls game so it dishes out punishment in heaps and then some. I have had my♥♥♥♥♥handed to me so many times and I still keep going back for more. What is great though, is it never feels truely unfair. In most occassions, if you die, its because you probably cocked up in some way, or you just arent ready for that fight yet. The combat is tight and responsive and absoloutely relentless in its punishment for mistakes. Learning how an enemy moves, what its strengths and weaknesses are and playing the patient game, waiting for that opening that will help you get the edge when you are up against a boss is probably one of the most rewarding experiences in a video game - providing it pays off of course.
Level design is outstanding, from craggy clifftops to dungeons and castle keeps and ramparts. It can be a maze of secrets, terrors and beauty and it never gets old or feels samey. There are so many secrets to discover in this game and so much to explore. I find myself traversing back through areas 5 or 6 times and still finding something different or something I missed before.
Sound design is also top notch and definately helps to immerse you. Whispers or wails can be generally creepy whilst the sounds of enemies and especially bosses just get better for each encounter.
I seriously cant recommend this game enough, even those that have tried previous Dark Souls titles and failed to get into them. Give Dark Souls 3 a shot. It is definately the most polished of the 3 and is just an incredible rewarding and yes at times infuriating experience. But its an experience that shouldn't be missed.
GRAPHICS - Holy *hit biscuts!
GAMEPLAY - Hold my beer!
LEVEL DESIGN - I'm lost, a little scared and if I'm honest, probably a little excited too.
SOUND - Probably one of the most terrifying aspects of the game.
OVERALL - It will tear your soul apart!

If Steam allowed for a neutral button instead of a like or dislike, that is what I would be clicking instead.
Pros:
1. Varied and Fast paced combat. You can bash the same buttons repeatedly or try and learn new amazing combos;
either playstyle is fun and satisfying.
2. Visually, pretty nice. Some enemies look really frightening and get you amped up for the fight!
3. Witch time is a real blast once you get used to it.
4. Enemies have subtle cues that telegraph attacks, and I really like the idea of audio cues.
Cons:
1. Horrible story and dull characters (with exception of Bayonetta). It isn't well told and the dialogue (in the english dub
atleast) is very mediocre (this coming from someone who generally loves over the top anime). There were some
geniunely funny moments though. Also, too many cutscenes...
2. The camera is very bad. I frequently found myself unable to find my bearings during fights with multiple enemies or
especially large bosses. Even the audio cues didn't help in really hectic moments and resulted in cheap deaths.
3.  Way too many cheap Quick time events, many of which are suddenly inserted into boss fights.
4.  Time wasting gimmicks - You can turn into a panther, but it felt forced and wasn't really used well. Same with the wall
climbing mechanic, which to me felt like it was added to artificially amp difficulty. Some boss fights also have their
own gimmicks, from turning the game into a shooter (using an aa gun) , to riding a bike and piloting a missile etc - all
of them felt like a gigantic waste of time and didn't really add anything to the game.
So there you go, my opinion of the game. I really enjoyed the combat but I thought it was let down by the camera and gimmicks. If you can get past the cons, the game is really enjoyable.
Personally, if you're looking for hack and slash games to play - I'd recommend two of platinum games' other outings over this one: Metal gear rising revengeance or Nier Automata, both of which are slick and a lot more fun. In fact Nier Automata has become one of my most favourite games of all time with near perfect combat and story - it too has its gimmicks, but they are very nicely executed!

This is one of my top 5 games of all time!
If you played EU/EW you have a very small idea of what the game is going to be like. I have a bit of time logged into those and thought I knew exactly what Xcom 2 was going to be like when it came out. Yes, you still move your soldiers from cover to cover and throw round after round at a superior alien race, but the whole atmosphere is different as you try and liberate a conquered and blinded planet. You most definitely are conquered. Fighting against superior weaponry and quite an advanced opponent, the game is a struggle, even in the latter stages. Cringing as you miss a 90% shot from 4 tiles away and cheering as you land a mile long snipe on a 13% shot through a car.
Xcom 2 used to suffer from a lot of bugs and unoptimized related issues but the Dev team has been incredibly diligent at ironing out the game into the master piece that is truly is. Along with releasing DLC that is just more epic each time you play. You know full well what you are getting when one comes out, they explain very thoroughly what is in each bundle and show case it in many pictures. So, don't be deceived by the nay-sayers.
Even if you don't like buying DLC, this game has such a great community that you don't have to spend an extra cent to get many more hours of enjoyment per mod. Long War is even releasing quite large mods which alter the game a surprising amount while remaining true to the basics of the game. I personally play with them all on after having played through Vanilla.
Pros;
- The vast amount of customization options with mods, dlc, and just the basic character customization tools.
- Destructible terrain
- The community with all its imagination.
- Continuing release of stellar content.
Cons;
- The massive framerate and lag issues on release (Which have since been fixed to an unnoticible thing of the past)
- Lack of an official Alien DLC with a handful of new aliens (Just would personally like to see some since there are a few missing from EU/EW)
TL;DR  This is a great game, give it a try and look at the workshop for variety. Carefully look at the DLC which is fairly priced in my opinion as it describes exactly what you get, contrary to many gripes. Different atmosphere from previous titles and continuing to get even more fun as they release more content. Any issues with the game have been ironed out or are easily fixed with a little patience and a well-mannered note to the Dev team! 10/10

I’m coming back to this review;
So I’ve been playing the game since early beta and I have to say it that there is no reason not to at least try it, now that it’s free.
It’s a team pvp brawler as you fight over objectives in your massive spaceships.
It is just plain better than Dreadnaught.
It looks great, sounds great and handles very friggin well.
Every ship in it feels unique and plays in its own way.
It’s free and the microtransactions are entirely cosmetics. Besides skins you can also unlock ships outright with money or speed up the unlocking process, but honestly, by doing that you are shooting yourself in the foot. You need to at least try every ship and understand how it works to have a chance at properly countering it, so the process of unlocking ships felt rewarding and meaningful.
The only complaint I might have over this game is its poor promotion and advertisement. I can respect that the developers chose to spend the resources on improving the game rather than advertisements, but the game does have a rather small community, so you might be waiting roughly 2 to 3 minutes to get a match, but each match does take roughly 20 minutes to complete, so it’s not that bad.
The game is constantly updated, the ships are being balanced, new modes are being added and it all feels fresh whenever I log in.
I've heard players complaining that the game crashes, but I've never had it happen to me, so I can't really say much on the matter.
Overall, I’d highly recommend this game.

Well, I just want to leave my review so far with almost three hours into the game. I have to say that I am really loving the experience. What sold me were two things, the option to create your own leaders and place them into the battle field and the whole large scale war aspect to the game. I love skirmish and I love being able to create my own characters in games.
There are several different modes to the game. You have story mode, free mode, and edit mode. In story mode you will get to choose between the two stories, the original and nightmare. I started off in the original since I’m new to the game and would like to start off from the beginning, but I am looking forward to nightmare because of the fantasy elements such as monsters!
In free mode you will be able to replay scenarios that you have unlocked. You will also be able to go online and play the several different modes with other players as well.
I love edit mode! I know I said it, but one thing I love in games is the option to customize your characters. In edit mode, you will be able to create your own custom leaders that you will be able to bring into battle. You will be able to level their skills, equip them, and grow attached to them! You can also send your custom leaders off to other battlefields where they may find special items and gain payment. You can also purchase equipment in the shop to upgrade your leaders gear as well. The shop offers skill books, armor, weapons, etc.
The combat is fun. Rather than your typical button masher, you get to control entire squads and command them to perform different attacks on enemy squads in a real-time strategy-like environment. The strategic elements to this game are also nice. I love being granted the choice to deploy your squads at the most crucial positions on the map.
Also, I have read many reviews about terrible performance, but I personally haven’t had any problems. My specs are: i7-6700, 32GB Ram, GTX 970, Windows 10.
So, based on my experience, I have to say that I would definitely recommend this game for those who like character customization, a different kind of real-time strategy experience, and for those who like war games mixed in with a bit of an RPG environment.

This is one of the most unique games I've ever played, both when it goes to esthetic and game mechanics. While it can be insanely difficult, grindy and frustratingly random at times, I still can't stress enough that everyone should give it a chance, as it's a one-of-a-kind experience.
The artstyle (hand-drawn 2D models and backgrounds), lovecraftian vibe and the contantly-present narrator are absolutely amazing, making it one of the most climatic games out there. I was absoluterly sold on it just after seeing the trailers and the game itself never failed when it goes to sustaining the mood of horror and misery. After many hours playing it and watching playthroughs of other people I still find it delighfully fresh and impactfull.
The gameplay, on the other hand, is a bit of a mixed bag. It consists of turn-based, team-of-four dungeon crawling with hero permadeath and can be slow and frustrating at times. The game basically tries to screw you over all of the time and makes sure you never get to a confort zone, where you can clear dungeons without fear of absolute disaster and loosing experienced characters. Even progression mechanics help little, as the challenges at the end of the road are always extremely hard and RNG might screw you over without any fault on your part. The radiant difficulty mode added a few months ago made the whole experience a little more accessible, but the end game is still absolutely brutal.
When playing I never actually aimed at beating the game, just knowing the absolute misery that awaits me with high difficulty bosses and the titular darkest dungeon. Still, for really hardcore players(/masochists?) this game is an absolute treat. For casuals, approaching it without unnecessary stress and using mods [!!!stacking inventory!!!] can make it very enjoyable too. In summary, I think this game is a must-buy, especially for the modest price The Red Hook asks for it. Aside of everything else, it's a piece of art that should be experienced personally, even if not encesseraly beaten.

Updated Proper Review:
I feel that most video games have lost weight, like a blind butcher's assistant I don't have a feel for the steaks. However, that all seemed to change with Darkest Dungeon because not only does it punish mistakes or poor strategy, it also has a nice little cemetery in the middle of the screen to remind you that you ♥♥♥♥ed up. Basically to say ' Hey, remember that one time you let Steve die to a heart attack because you neglected his stress? Well here he is immortalized for you so you can realize your mistake.' At this point I will state that you will make mistakes and you will at some point lose a party member or whole party. Regardless, I always found myself coming back for more, like some S&M slave eager for their routine flogging. Slowly learning more and more about how the game works through my failures. Then when you start feeling comfortable and go up to veteran or champion levels you find yourself knocked down a peg and having to adapt to learn new strategies based on the new ways the same or new things are thrown at you.
For example, I found myself not really using holy water. Then when I found myself in champion level dungeons I decided to use it because the dots of blights and bleeds were really starting to hurt. I can honestly tell you that it was making a difference because every time I wasn't dodging I wasn't  always getting a blight or bleed debuff. I overall applaud this progression of gameplay but it is very easy to see it as unfair if you don't experiment with everything at your disposal when you hit a strategic wall.
RNG will both save you and you kill but it all evens itself out if you prepare whether it's with holy water or buffing up your stats at a campfire before a boss battle. It all increases your chance of success one way or another and if looks bleak you can also abandon the quest to live another day so it never really seems unfair.
The only real complaint I have is it can seem quite grindy and overly long and it can be exacerbated if you find yourself losing a lot of party members. However, there are catch up mechanics when you upgrade the stagecoach. You can get higher level characters to come in for recruitment, so you're not necessarily starting at square one if that does happen.
Overall: 9/10

- Relatively short story at around 30 hours compared to the 70-80 you get out of a similarly priced Souls game

I was a fan of the first release of the game, though I know not many people would be that fond of it.  If it were like that version, just with the PC tweaks, i'd give it a recommendation.  The problem is, however, that this was not a proper PC port.  They released the game and just kind of gave up on updates, so you need to do tweaks first to get it to actually work, then operate with the idea that you are just going to have random crashes.  If they fixed them, the game could be salavaged.
Now, for the changes from the PS3/Xbox360 release, and how I feel about them.  Obviously the big one is the graphics, always good to get a little more eye candy in, and they did so without messing up performance, which has also been heavily overhauled, allowing the game to run a lot smoother.
The new campaign has some promise, taking a full on fantasy route, and being able to field your own subbordinate commanders is kind of cool.  They diversified some of the units you face, making it harder to just steamroll with heavy calvary, and the new giant commanders, while somewhat out of place, do add to the challenge.  It seems like you need more forces than you used to, but it dosen't feel like an undue ramp up of difficulty.  If you really want to try it, I'd recommend going for a console release, as this version is just too prone to issues.

I highly recommend this game, if you just want a game where you feel powerful, and are given a chance to be playful with loads and loads of different troop-types. I'm having great fun tearing up armies with both pikemen, two-handed swords and horses, which each have many ethnic variations, such as China Spearmen and Ninjas. The horses are difficult, but once you get the hang of them, they're a powerful tool, and great fun to ride.
Granted, the game is super easy for a long time, while you're training and gearing up your troops, but in order to learn how to utilize multiple mercenaries in one battle, you're going to need practice. I highly recommend you to try leveling up your different "troop books" evenly. At least 4-5 different types. Not only because variety is nice, but if you overlevel your main troops, the game gets a bit boring, since you'll run over everything in the beginning, and then later you'll have a hard time leveling up the ones you neglected, since they're now too weak (then you have to do extra easy scenarios with 1 star, wasting time). I forego training Bows and Knives, since they hardly matter, once you have the stronger troop-types trained up. They are good for runs where you need speedy units, to end the battle quickly across a long stretch, though, but I use my horses for that.
It is VERY satisfying to be running against a huge army, with your 30 trusty swordsmen, and time your attack perfectly, to rip them all to pieces. You just can't help being sucked into it. "Come on! We have 50 seconds to find the Base Commander and kill him, to get his sweet, sweet loot! Run b*****ds!"
Actually, the game is worth the money (especially on sale), just for the sheer joy of hearing the way the bartender pronounces the word "mercenary", which he does a lot. My heart sings a little every time, and I feel an extra $1 of worth for the game. He's the gift that keeps on giving.
The game is a port from PS3, and several people are complaining that their PC rigs cannot handle the game. I, however, am having zero performance problems. This is my rig:
ASUS RoG laptop
Intel i7 Quadcore 2.6 GHz
Geforce 980M 4GB
16GB DDR3
Granted, in the game configuration I turned off vSync, AO (Ambient Occlusion; hate it) and Anti-aliasing, and set Depth of Field to Low (cuz I hate it). To compensate, I force (override) Anti-aliasing (x4) in the Nvidia control panel, as well as Triple Buffering and "Fast" vSync. It seems to work better. Everything is peachy in-game, and the videos have zero tearing now.
There's an intermittent stutter, but that goes away once I ALT-TAB out and kill "Steam Client Bootstrapper" from the Task Manager. But that's a general problem. I have the same problem with Grim Dawn, Titan Quest, Path of Exile, you name it.
If you're still having problems, try turning off the Steam overlay. You can remove it in the Steam settings.

Metal Slug X or as otherwise know as Metal Slug 2 superior version is the second title in the series that came to steam, so let's look into it.
Story wise it takes place two years after the first Metal Slug and you are once again tasked to defeat the evil General Morden who has now formed an alliance with aliens.
Metal Slug X is very similar to the other titles in the series, but this time it included new vehicles, weapons, character transformations and a supporting characters.
The gameplay is still the same as the other titles, there's nothing new to learn, so if you played the previous title you already know what to expect.
The game is still a ton of fun and I had a fantastic time playing through the 6 missions and even went to replay the game a second time on a higher difficulty.
The game ran perfectly apart from one minor stutter problem during the final boss battle, but that only happened once.
I still think for me this is the weakest in the series, but it's still a ton of fun and worth buying at full price.
Final Rating:
7/10 - Worth Playing

This is my second review on this game after actually being able to progress into the game. Whether some of you find this relevant or irrelevant ACU is very good in some areas but fails terribly after recent games in the series.

THE BAD
1. COMBAT
They had reduced the combat to you frantically mashing the attack button while your assassin seems to be stuck in this "Its okay I have all the time in the world, Im not gonna die!" Mindset. And once you swing, depending on the level of the enemy, your attack is deflected. Oh thats not working let me use my pistol! Nope the enemy somersaults and you miss. At this point another enemy is already attacking you and youre out of medicine to heal, so, you decide to drop a smoke bomb and run away. But you cant because youre getting spammed with attacks from each side. Then you die.
-There are no instant kills after you counter.
-There are no instant kill streak chains.
Basically I dont feel like the assassin bad♥♥♥♥♥I once was in other game previously.
Like in Brotherhood when they introduced the Kill Streaks and the offensive guard breaks.
Im sure Ive missed some negative thins about the combat but you get the point. Im frustrated.
2. PARKOUR
The brand new descent system! Very innovative actually. But most of the glitches I have encountered were because of this. I "gracefully" descend into the wall. At the speed of light. One minute Im on top the next Im inside the wall or a chimney. Time to reload the last check point or restart the game. Although thats not the only free running glitch Ive encountered. There are the typical AC frustrations that come up with the parkour sytem. Its like this in EVERYGAME. I guess weve just accepted it and moved on. And so will I with this rant of a review.
3. Performance Issues/NPC glitches.
The most discussed topic among the Steam community is the performance of this game. How terribly optimized it is for pc. So I dont feel the need to go into depth here other than to say that you cant run this game in ultra unless you have amazing stuff in your pc. I can only get about 20-35 fps on high settings. Cant use any AA. So for me its playable but the framedrops and stutters seriously need to go. This is why my game crashes every now and then. And why I just say F**K it and stop playing altogether.
As always npcs pop up out of nowhere and climb up on objects or get stuck in the ground.
Ive carried on to long with the bad so here is the good.
THE GOOD.

This is a revised review that I did returning to this game and see how much has changed since a year ago when I first tried it and was sorely disappointed. Performance of this game has been greatly increased and optimizations have removed the lags and clunkiness of the first time I tried it. The visual fidelity has been somewhat lowered but it's worth it since game still looks great and better performance/gameplay is always preferred to make a game more accessible for newcomers. Gameplay wise I this time around enjoyed it a lot more, Ships are faster and more classes of ships etc. Have been introduced. Everything is much more polished and in my opinion so is gameplay. This is a double edged sword however and this game has been losing players due to the fans of the original early access game being used to that gameplay, now felt enraged about the new changes. However I argue that if you are a newcomer and never tried the old gameplay, it will not cause trouble for you. This game has been streamlined to appeal more for the masses while still trying to maintain the tactical skill aspects, albeit making it less so to broaden the appeal. The original early access game was catering to very niche market IMHO. Of hardcore players whose skill in the game would quickly alienate newcomers and the game mechanics just taking too much patience to master. Also the devs have been experimenting quite randomly with ideas and the core game has been almost overhauled so many times that alot of the original community has moved on due to frustration. Again this is not an issue to the newcomers who don't know what revisions of game have been in the past. In the past player numbers were dropped so low it would take 10-15 minutes to get into a match. This has been remedied by devs by introducing bots to fill the gaps caused by fewer people populating servers. Now I can get into a match in about 30 seconds. Of course playing mixed battles with bots and humans is not ideal for this type of game but it is the only solution now in an effort to save this game from dying out while trying to increse player numbers. In my opinion they have succeeded as now the game is not a murder fest of extreme players who were born with this game at hand and are like mutant freaks with superpowers and annihilate every poor newcomer in seconds. I too can now score satisfying kills and help me get engaged in this game more. Like I said, this time I enjoyed it. To the HC gamer this is an abomination because they are allergic to casual gamers who wander to a new game to try it out. They want to stick to their niche and in their uber clans and don't want noobs to rain on their competetive superiority. I understand that HC gamers do need games for themselves where they can feel at the top of the foodchain but also there needs to be accessibility for noobs or the game will die out. If you are a fan of the early access game, this is propably not for you. But if you are a newcomer, this is a fine alternative to dreadnought since the gameplay is completely different and instead of competing with dreadnought, they complement each other in capital ship battle market. We don't have many of those as you know. There are few concerns about the future of this game though, and that is the low player numbers caused by the devs releasing this game in a too unfinished state to begin with. The long dev cycle and many iterations and changes this game has had, has caused many to move on thus leading to decline in player numbers. Like said before, the added bots to fill the loss of human players has smoothed it out a bit and made the game easier to get into. But it's not a perfect solution of course.
You can see my original review below if you are interested to compare my experience with this game now.
My old review a year ago:
Man I really, really want to dig this game, but alas, as it is now, I can't. I got this on early access because I can't wait for Dreadnought to be finished. I'm a sucker for space combat but especially for Capital class combat. Sadly, this is a game that  has wonderful pontential graphically, cool looking ships etc. But fails in my experience utterly to convey a Capital class battle. Your ship, no matter how many miles/kilometers long behemoth your'e riding with, moves slow as a Capital ship but takes hits like a small scout class ship. I mean literally not even like a fighter, but rather a scout. The lifespan of these ships once engaged in battle are less than a minute. Or then I'm just such a bad player in this game which is totally possible. The thing for me is, there's potential in game mechanics, such as turning your ship around to present the enemy with fresh hull plating and shields, but because the ships are so slow, I never lived long enough to use that mechanic effectively. If there was TIME for a player to actually learn to get used to the nuances of gameplay mechanics here, it would make for a lot better experience plus make the battles actually feel like Capital Class ships dueling it out. The other problem I think is the scale of battles. There's no way to hide behind objects or use the aforementioned tactics when 5 other capital ships are missiling and lasering your ship from every angle like a sitting duck. There's simply too many capital class ships allowed in the same map causing mayhem rather than cool and balanced gameplay. Maybe this game needs introduction of bot fighter jets and bombers to balance things out, I don't know but for me the game is insanely poorly balanced at it's current state.
The other thing to mention is atmosphere. This is a game that has the elements for great atmosphere, but I found it all lacking in a big way. The game felt like it has no soul to me. I could not care for my crew one bit. And they are not that different balance wise to even take notice. So Capital class whimper battle combined with lots of dying and respawning, having to move all that way back to battle like a sloth only to be executed to pieces upon arrival in 30 seconds, combined with soulles atmosphere killed the experience for me. I'm not a hardcore player but rather a casual one and that's possibly why I could'nt enjoy the game even when I wanted to. However there are games out there that give a sense of rewarding to both n00bs and elitists alike, so it should'nt be impossible to achieve. I hope this game will evolve into a serious contender for Dreadnought. Consider waiting a while before getting into t,his game unless you're a completely fanatic and hardcore player. Perhaps not the best game for people with real lives on the side, takes too much learning to become effective for a total casual gamer like myself. Now that does not mean it's a bad game, just wasn't for me.

I personally love this game. It is a MOBA at heart, but if you don't like traditional MOBAs don't be discouraged. This game is straighforward but manages to be interesting all the same. It is also VERY well balanced, and I will explain what I mean below.
SKILL BASED COMBAT
This game is all about skill. The ships all have tradeoffs, so that no ship is truly better than another. Let's take the overseer, a sniper ship with a long range laser gun. It is weak at short range. You would think it would be OP since, space is space and there is a lot of open areas. Wrong. There are many ways to close or combat it, just like any other ship. Bombers, stealth ships, fast agile ships and blink drives all give sniper ships trouble.
Ship Classes
I like to divide the ships into the game into 4 roles:
Combat Cruisers
-Medium range ships that take decent beatings and dish out decent damage at , very balanced (ex. Reaper or Venturer)
Dreadnoughts
-Big slow and heavily armed for short ranged (ex. Colossus or Leviathan)
Destroyers
-Fast small ships with varying firepower and interesting abilities[I include stealth ships] (ex. Ghost or Raider)
Support Ships
-All shapes and sizes, these odd ships fill specialty roles that can make a real difference when supporting the damage classes above [snipers are support, not carry] (ex Protector or the Paragon)
So some people complain about how some ships are good and some suck. This is not the case, it's just they do not have any skills besides brawling and/or straight yolo rushes. Fights are quite nuanced between skilled players. Each ship has it's own playstyle. Most players use a few "meta" ships, which are quite strong and have simple gameplay. These are usually combat cruisers or dreadnoughts. I love using specialty ships and ships with hidden potential to counter cruisers, which make up the bulk of players. I also end up being called a hacking ♥♥♥♥♥♥ a lot. Name of the game: Skill and playstyle> Quote "Meta" ships

This game can be summed up rather easily - World of Warships with Dota gameplay using Capital ships in space. PvP only, only one map to select from, very small player pool, buggy match-making system means pretty much zero games unless you live in the USA. Other than that, the tutorial is excellent, the gameplay is quite good, combat is smooth and makes sense. The ship designs are excellent with an enormous level of customisation available. Though the engine is enormously buggy, getting the game to even run is an excercise in playing russian roulette with your computer. Once running is it smooth without issues though (for me at least)
The worst thing about this however is that it is pay to win. Only a small fraction of the game is available to players and the rest is gained through in-game microtransactions. You can purchase experience and upgrade points on top of this. For a PvP style team game this is the worst possible decision that could be made. What makes them even worse is that these are not a few cents or a few dollars here and there, most of them are quite pricey, and combined with the very expensive DLCs and the initial cost of the game, makes this an expensive game if you want to stand even the remotest chance in battle.
I would have given this a thumbs up in spite of a few issues it had if it were not for the pay to win. Slick game, well made, but utterly fails at the end of the day.

I know the descriptions say its an alien, but I couldn't help but think it looked like an apple, and that it would probably fall pretty close to the tree, because, you know, proverbs.  No, I don't mean like in the bible, I mean in the colloquial homespun wisdom passed down by old people on rocking chairs.  Ever wonder just why these wise old folks are almost always found in rocking chairs?  I do.  I wonder if maybe they're not all that wise after all, if maybe for some reason we are all just programmed to accept anything said by someone in a rocking chair as being wise.  Now that I think about it, my grandmother would sit in her rocker and by golly it seemed like all she could do was spout pearls of wisdom, but I'll tell you this much.  As soon as she got up from that chair, bam, we put her♥♥♥♥♥in a home.  Just kidding about the home, the truth is we had her put down.  Such is the way of our people.
So, yeah. it's well worth the time to play The Old Tree, it is a pretty game, little bit like something Amanita would do, also reminds me of The Plan.  I give it something out of something else.  Whatever, I can't do maths.
