People are giving this game bad reviews because there wasn't any major update.
But what they don't realise is that devs are releasing Nightly build (beta of beta).
Nightly build is nice feature because we can play with new features that aren't in game and maybe won't ever be.
Nightly build has some great features like new Novakid race , advanced combat, lot of new items, ship AI and way more stuff that is not yet in game.It's lot of fun after you run out of things to do in normal game.
But be warned!!! Nightly build is REALY BROKEN some times, it's beta version of beta version game so bugs, glitches and fps drops are expected.
Still a lot of fun to play in your free time, exploration is basicly infinite because of 5 sectors that have very large amount of solar systems that usually have around 3-4 planets so going over them all is pretty much impossible.
So for my conclusion:
Pros:
+6 playable races ,each with their own culture
+Lot of planets and solar systems to explore
+Lots of collectables (Horse head,outfits,playable musical instruments ...)
+Soundtrack is incredible
+Random types of enemies
+Techs (Dash, power jump, power ball from Metroid, Mech ...)
+Big selection of weapons and guns (guns can be optained on Avian ship that you find by finding big anchor on the ground)
+Armor (You will mostly use Racial armor but you can buy blueprints of armor of other races)
+Decoration (Lots of stuff for decoration, but you must find it first)
+Dungeons (Racial dungeons are designed by racial culture, like Avian Dungeon is designed to look really religious,Glitch have medieval castles with king and knights,Humans have prisons .... Oh and there is a Sewer Dungeon with poop enemies :D)
+Progression (You can progress in game by beating Bosses, crafting upgrades to be able to craft items with better ores)
+Mini-Bosses (Mini-bosses are randomly generated big enemies that are really powerful and are fairly challenging, but they drop rare items)
+Uncommon and Legendary Weapons (Rare weapons have special function like setting enemies on fire,poisoning them ect., Legendary weapons are signature like Tesla staff shooting lightning bolts....)
+When Floran (Plant people that are hunters) describe something it's usually pretty funny ("Fishface! Away!")
+Nightly build (It's broken, but fun)
+Stars falling at night look beautiful
+2D graphics looks nice in this game
Cons:
-Bosses (They are easy to beat if you wall yourself in and poke them with a stick through tiny space)
-Combat (Enemies are trying to ram into you, some have projectiles, some just charge) BUT!!! In Nightly build enemies AI is improved significantly and they are real danger to you.
-Fps drops sometimes but thats because of Beta or my computer :)
-Sometimes it's hard to get Nightly build to work
-Enemies are sometimes annoying (Like when you're climbing anchor to get to Avian ship and bird comes and knocks you down,DAMN YOU BIRD!!!)

I have been reading a lot of the supposed "most helpful reviews" and I must say I disagree strongly. Also, the fact that the "most helpful" review not only has a lower percentage of people who found it helpful, but has fewer people who voted on it period, means that something is drastically wrong with the reviews most people will see when they look at this game.
Now, many of the "most helpful" reviews have very outdated information. First off, the game is very much in full development mode, and the developers are adding in content by the bucket full, and revamping the game. The game already has a significant amount of content in it, and because of that, I find the fact that its developers say it's still not even close to finished very promising. Second, a lot of the reviews say that time stops when you go to other planets, this is NOT true at all anymore. The game has progressed a lot since most negative reviews have been written, and a lot of the things they say are either no longer true, or never were.
I find this game to only have a few things I would actually change about it:
The fact that all wood is "unrefined" and you don't get different kinds of wood from different trees. HOWEVER, there are about 200+ different kinds of trees, and the developers have already said they would eventually make all kinds of wood different.
The modding system leaves something to be desired, but it is very unfinished according to the developers, and it is already one of the best modding systems I've seen to date that actually don't restrict you in what you can do. It is written in lua, and can be easily decompiled using a tool they have already provided, meaning one can potentially use the system to make an entirely different game if they wanted to, and still have it launch from starbound's launcher.
Also, there is a good chance for save corruption, but the bug causing them to be corrupted is ALREADY FIXED in the latest nightly build. And, even when saves are corrupted, it is normally only the player's location that has changed, meaning that if you remember where you were before, you can easily return there.
I love this game, and I feel that it has a growing communiy, with tons of potential. On a final note, for the people who say this game is as easy as minecraft, I say I must disagree. While not as hard as Terraria can get, it is not as easy as unmodded minecraft, unless you play minecraft on hard, which is actually a challenge for some of us who have slowler computers.

Going into this I only had one real question.  Is it like Dynasty Warriors?  Short answer: No.  There are elements you will know from other Warrior titles but This game differs in one key aspect.  You are not a badass warrior who wipes out 1000s of soldiers per battle single handedly.   Instead you are a commander of a squad of soldiers and your Squad, with you along side them,  fight hordes of enemies.
I went into it thinking the squad was just a neat gimmick but I would still be attacking wiht my main character.  Instead you issue generic fight commands and decide the opportune times for your entire squad to unleash a special attack.  You lose a bit of the flair and spectacle you get in the other Warrior games but it is replaced with a battle that is larger in scale.
Your individual character, while important, is nowhere near as lionized as any character from traditional wariror series.  You play as a mercenary that you personally create similar to how you create custom officers in other Wariror games.  You will find your armor sets to be very limited in character creation but that is because pieces of armor have actual statistical effects.  In the course of the game you will buy armor and equiping it changes your appearance.  There are main characters but you never play as them, as far as I can tell,  instead they appear in certain battles and will be fighting alongside, or against, you.  You are very much made to feel as a cog in a giant war machine in the endless battles of the Hundred years war.
So to ask "is this like Dynasty Warriors?" is actually a mroe complicated question than a short yes or no can provide.  I'm a huge fan of the Warrior series and have only had problems with one game due to porting issues rather than the game itself.  I feel at home in this game coming from that background but the changes may turn off some who like the more story driven focus on specific characters.  To me the change is a refreshing new take on the Warriors gameplay and an intersting new setting.  I actually think it feels better having a group of people fighting instead of just having 1 single guy completely annialate armies.

After reading all of the reviews for this game I feel obligated to say how I feel.
This is one of my most favorite games. The way the game makes you feel about both the enemys and your own heroes is freaking amazing. You want your heroes to live, and when they die it is heartbreaking. You will feel damn near depressed at the thought of it. Notice how I said AND and not IF your heroes die. That's because at some point they will and it is also why I felt I needed to say something about it.
I see to many people complaining about this game being to much rng and when they lose apart of their "dream squad" that the game needs to change.
This is the most wrong thing I think I have ever seen for two reasons.
1. This is a Lovecraftian horror game. The whole point is to create a sense of helplessness and how much you do not matter in this world of ungoldy abominations.
2. One of the main conflicts of this game is dealing with the crap that comes you way. One of the first paragraphs you read on the title screen says :
"Darkest Dungeon is about making the best of a bad situation. Quests will fail or must be abandoned. Heroes will die. And when they die, they stay dead. Progress autosaves constantly, so actions are permanent."
"The game expects a lot out of you. How far will you push your adventurers? How much are you willing to risk in your quest to restore the Hamlet? What will you sacrifice to save the life of your favourite hero?"
This sense of helplessness is also what makes winning feel so good when you know that you overcame what seemed to be impossible obsticles and become stronger throughout he game.
So please, do not judge this game about being so rng when it is trying to share a good lesson: You must press on.

Let me preface that 6 months ago, I loved playing Darkest Dungeon. The random number generator could be brutal at times, but those horrible encounters were offset by glimmering moments of hope (lucky RNG) and good old fashioned strategy.
When the Crimson Court update came out, I decided to start playing again. I hadn't tried Radiant mode (having previously done both normal and Stygian), so I thought I'd experience the "easy mode" with new content. And then Dismas died in the second encounter (two brigands) during the introduction quest.
A little annoying, but it happens (OK, it had never happened before). I started a new campaign not wanting to deal with being a man down before the game actually began. Got through the brigand encounters, started the first ruins quest, and Dismas dies again. At that point, I'm feeling annoyed. So I start a third campaign from scratch, get through the brigand and ruins tutorial quests, start a medium foray into the ruins, and Reynauld dies.
Now I neither know nor care if this was just terrible luck or an intended update to increase the game's "challenge". What I do know is it was not fun and that I can no longer recommend a once great game. Games are supposed to be fun, and challenging games are supposed to be fun and challenging. And since there is nothing I can do beside roll another campaign and hope for the best, Darkest Dungeon has become neither fun nor challenging... just unpleasant.

Has potential but is severely lacking substance.  Definitely not worth $10.  With all the references to Uplink, I cannot figure out why reviews are "overwhelmingly positive", as this game falls seriously short of Uplink.
The storyline is cliché, and not really immersive.
The systems you "hack" lack diversity and content.
The "hacking" itself is extremely easy, and consists of essentially repeating the same commands over and over, and the ports simply force you to repeat those commands even more.
There are no real hardware or software upgrades, and the "RAM" defined is hardly sufficient for what are apparently the most memory-intensive programs ever (I can't figure out why a few character note uses many MB).
The risk is nonexistent.  If you do happen to get traced, you can easily reset your IP (which inexplicably reboots your machine), and continue like nothing happened.
Log deletion is trivial, as a simple rm * deletes all logs and you don't even need to consider a disconnect log entry, because it will not be created.
No networks or complex systems, no banks; there are mobile devices but they might as well not even be locked for how easy it is to get into them.
Command line adds nothing to the game except what seems to be an attempt to hide the lack of content by introducing a layer of tedium.  (Typing basic unix commands doesn't qualify as hacking.)
Network map is a cluster♥♥♥♥.

Hmmm what can I say about Bayonetta?  The characters are kind of cheesy and there's no big surprises or twists in the story but that's part of the charm of the genre.  Enter ridiculously overpowered badass, ridiculously overpowered badass overcomes an increasingly ridiculously overpowered horde of behemoth enemies, up to and including deities. Bayonetta's cocky attitude and wit is a great addition to that formula.  It's pretty satisfying to lay a major beat down after talking crazy to a giant angel.  Speaking of delivering beat downs, the combat in this game is smooth and sweet.  You can dodge in the middle of combos by timing correctly, and when you pull off a successful last minute dodge, time slows down giving you even more free shots at the bad guys.  Once you master a few combos and collect a few different weapons, you move in and out of whippin angel butt with style and grace.  I also like how you can go back and replay every chapter with the items you've collected and try to max out your ratings for each battle.  Gives the game a ton of replayability.  Absolutely recommend this game.  I hope they consider porting the sequel to PC somewhere down the road too!

If you've played the other Souls games, you'll know what to expect, but there are some tweaks here and there that really streamline the player experience. For example: holding down the run button will automatically start running again once you regain your stamina. The addition of weapon skills adds even more depth to one of the most flexible combat systems in any game series, and the Firelink Shrine is such a great hub level, especially once you start NPC questlines and populate it a bit. The voice acting is top-knotch and much of the cast from the previous games returns. The boss music is just breathtaking, although some of the early bosses are pretty easy, especially with coop support. DS3 might not be the best entry point into the series for a new player, since there are all sorts of callbacks and tie-ins to the lore of the first game, and the tutorial boss can be a major stalling point if you aren't familiar with Souls combat but the game design is really good at teaching lessons, basically by preventing you from progressing until your skill level improves. Also it runs at 800x600 on an AMD integrated chip LMAO

Had this game on the PS3 and loved it and now that its on PC and improved it feels like the great hack and slash game I played years ago. For anyone having trouble with crashing and stuttering set these settings to the following:
Shaders - Low
Particles - Low
Motion Blur & Light Shaft - Low (Dont know if impacts performance, just my personal preference)
Most important of all set the games .exe files to compatibility mode for windows 7.
Doing those above things has meant I can enjoy this game for hours on end with no crashes, lag or stuttering and the graphics are still far better than when it came out on the older consoles.
The new features are good although I have yet to try the Nightmare Mode, but do make good use of the new "Station" feature that allows you to have upto 2 mercenaries in other peoples games to collect money, loot and a chance to get a rare item from another player if they beat them. However getting over 20k SP points from a single 12hr outing seems to take away some of the challenge of levelling your own troops, although you can simply ignore sending your own mercs' into other peoples games and just play the game like normal.
My most favoured addition is creating new mercenaries and ordering them what to do (cap bases, hunt enemy mercs, etc) as they can take some pressure off of you and also be able to form a large army with them. This adds some flexibility to how you do missions and enables you to use the other heroes in the game if you have them in your party at start of the battle (so far I have unlocked Marie and Phillipe le Bon to use in the squad and to actually play as them too)
Overall I think this game is fantastic and would recommend it to anyone who like a good hack and slash game, although get it while its in sale (got mine in the Summer Sale and 60% off) as no game is worth £50 imo.

Bladestorm is a weird mash between Total War and Musou game, very weird to control at first but super fun once you learn how everything works. This port isn't totally unplayable as some of the reviews will lead you to believe (PS4 port instead of PS3, online multiplayer included) but still has some issues to improve on. Koei doesn't patch their games 99% of the time so these issues won't be fixed but if you're willing to look past some minor flaws that don't hamper gameplay much its a enjoyable and rather lengthy game. Here are the issues with the port:
- No controller button prompts
- Mediocre optimization, framerate is about 30-40 FPS during battles maxed out with a GTX 970 and FX-8370
- Opening cutscene to Nightmare Mode has prerendered japanese text instead of english text if you have the JP voice option selected
- Will crash alot unless you have Windows 7 Compatibility Mode turned on (still crashes occasionally with it on but not nearly as much)

Have you ever wished your graphic adventure games had a little more action? Or that your platformers required a bit more puzzle solving? Well, Insecticide is here, kind of a Reese's Peanut Butter Cup of point-and-click and action games. Unfortunately, only one of these elements turned out well. While the investigative segments of the game are a blast from the past, the platforming and combat are clunky and frustrating.
Developer Crackpot has created an engaging world for Insecticide. The game is set in an alternate future where insects have evolved past humans and become humanoids. People are still around, but they have devolved into hominids and are barely surviving in the sewers. Many crime story clichés have been written into the script, but videogames can usually get away with reusing material movies ran into the ground years ago. You've got your grumpy police chief, your stakeout mission, your conspiracy that goes all the way to the upper echelons of power… All of the dialogue is peppered with insect puns that may have you rolling your eyes at first, but they end up being endearing. The game is often funny, and there are lots of geeky references to 60s sci-fi movies and other areas of pop culture.
The player controls Detective Chrys Liszt as she investigates a possible homicide at a powerful corporation. To catch the bad guys, she alternates investigating crime scenes and chasing suspects. The crime scenes feature tried-and-true point-and-click gameplay and it's done very well. These portions of the game are fun, funny, and will provide a decent challenge to adventure gamers -- in fact, the game was created by LucasArts veterans who clearly know the genre.
When the action kicks in, though, the fun checks out. Chrys can only fire one shot every few seconds, so forget about intense shootouts. And while she has a decent inventory of weapons, there's no way to switch them quickly. Either the Y button can cycle through them one at a time, or you can remove your hand from the fire button and select the gun you want with the stylus. She also turns at snail speed, so trying to dodge enemy fire is fruitless.
The investigation sequences are really fun. The platforming...not so much.
The graphics during the action sequences are pretty drab, and it can be hard to tell where you need to go next. Even if you do know, the camera might not let you get a good look. The game is also very dark, so playing on an old-school original DS phat might give you problems.
There are unforgiving tightrope-walking segments that you'll be playing many times over. Most of the time the game respawns you near the place of your demise, but there are a few sections that send you too far back and force you to repeat frustrating areas over and over again.
For the most part the audio is a quality affair. The voice acting is great, and the music is fully orchestrated. The soundtrack is a mix of seedy jazz and more intense, action-packed stuff. But the music doesn't loop smoothly, so it stutters briefly as it restarts, like a DVD menu. Sound effects are often missing at key moments. At one point Chrys defeats a giant, mechanical spider boss, but the beast disappears from the screen without any noise, any explosion, nothing.
THE VERDICT
This one is a real heartbreaker. I really wanted to score it higher, but the action sequences get in the way of what could have been an extremely enjoyable adventure game. Crackpot has created an engrossing world with Insecticide, so maybe a sequel will focus more on pointing and clicking than frustrating and agitating. There are a lot of places this franchise could go, with plenty of interesting characters to develop. Sometimes a game should just do one thing, and do it well.

One of my all-time favourite games, if you love strategy games with plenty to manage and keep in mind, I couldn't recommend it enough. Currently having great fun discovering the amazing amount of extra content in the DLC, Crimson Court.
+Great artstyle.
+Great character/enemy concepts (DLC adds vampires based on mosquitoes, for example).
+Fantastic dynamic soundtrack that gets more intense as light levels drop, really adds to the atmosphere.
+Narrator Wayne June provides a jaw-droppingly satisfying performance.
+Tight inventory management, stress management, resource management, party management etc. Forces you to make tough but satisfying prioritisation decisions based on your situation.
+Game is IMO perfectly balanced so that you can make almost any situation work with enough skill and a maybe a lil luck. You can put your healer at the front of the group if you gear your party for that. If you think a class is bad, it's because you haven't used them enough.
While, yes, each area has maybe 20-30 distinct encounters that you will see time and again, each encounter is tailored to provide its own challenge in prioritisation based on who you're using, what attacks they have, which enemies are in what position, who ends up going before who, and what state your heroes are in at the time, among other subtle factors (phobias, buffs, debuffs, trinkets, etc etc). Having a team that can move the enemies out of position gives you much different options for strategy comparted to having a team that stuns well, for example.
I would definitely recommend skimming through a couple videos seeing how people prepare for different areas, and how well it goes. You can find detailed spreadsheets giving outlines for what to bring where. Youtuber Baertaffy has played this game so much, and at the start of his videos he explains who and what he's bringing where and why. Maybe watch the first few minutes of a handful of his DD videos to get an idea of how to prepare. If you're unsure on what to bring, overpreparation is a safe bet. Bring lots of food and shovels.

Get ready for another one hour of run and gun action with Metal Slug. You know, once I've written a review of one Metal Slug, I could just copy and paste them for all the games. I know the developers sure did when it comes to art and animation, but with a style so great it was the wise choice to use assets from the previous game. Metal Slug X is a modified version of Metal Slug 2 rather than the tenth game in the series.
There's a lot new to the game that's fresh from its predecessor. Metal Slug X becomes a parody of itself. Rather than a game full of strict action and a few chuckles here and there, this game brings charming absurdity and laughs.
The story is simple, again the world is in danger and you need to stop him. Like all Metal Slug games, you can bring a friend for some cooperative action. There is online multiplayer, but no one is using it. The big twist with Metal Slug X is rather than saving a world, you turn unite with the enemy to face the greater evil evil.
At the start, there is get four characters to chose from. There seems to be no difference between them and if you get a game over, you can chose a new character. Each character starts with a pistol, a few throwable bombs and a jump. You can fire three directions and four if you jump. Getting close to an enemy and attacking will perform a melee slash which is also good for cutting larger projectiles out of the air.
As you progress through the levels you'll face off against mummies, and later wall crawling sewer ghouls. Mummies, mummy dogs and bats have the ability to turn your character into a mummy. This constricts you to a pistol and slow movement. Jumps feel stiff because you're wrapped in bandages. Rather than throwing a grenade, you can throw your head instead.
Along the way, you'll pick up items for points; things like fruit, pigs, cats and medals. If you eat too much food, pigs or cats your character will become fat. This makes you move slow, but your bullets are much larger as a trade off. It will still get you killed in an instant. Metal Slug is a sluggish game in general, but getting hindered by obesity is a sure fire death sentence.
The game in general is just a death sentence, but a fun one. The screen fills with enemies and projectiles so its easy to die with how stiff your character moves. Its all that great animation weighing you down. Since this is a home version of the arcade game, there are several different difficulties and a free play mode that gives you unlimited continues. Once you complete the game, it tells you how many continues you used and then you can multiply that by quarters you would have spent in an arcade machine.
There are more vehicles in this game than the previous. Instead of just the Metal Slug tank, you can now drive a camel through the streets. The camel performs a lot like the Metal Slug, but you're susceptible to dying while you're mounted the hump. The a new mech is a good one to pilot because it has twin guns that are more accurate than the tank or the camel. Last, but not least is the jet that lets you fly around and fire missiles.
Another thing that sets this game apart from other Metal Slugs are the environments. The first level is in an Arabian city. The second level is through a mine that turns into catacombs. There are rehashed cities from the previous game, but they manage to feel fresh with cars that explode up rather than get crushed under tank treads. There is a dark sewer and an alien base.
A few of the bosses are recycled from the original game and pallet swapped. Other bosses are brand new. Things like a giant metal worm that's eating a stone tower that forces you to keep jumping up or die. You'll find many bosses that rely on you having to leap into the air and shoot down at them.
One thing I did notice about the bosses is how many bullets they takes. When you need to shoot them with a pistol and push the button for each and every bullet you fire, it turns into a test of endurance. The incentive to put another quarter into the game when its game over is the fact that a heavy machine gun drops for your next game.
The heavy machine gun fires a burst to make it more effective than just a pistol. All the previous weapons are back; the shotgun rips enemies in half at short range, flame thrower with the best burn animation of any game, rocket launcher that steers projectiles toward an enemy and a few others. A lot more weapons make their debut. A bouncing ball gun. Chasing rockets that are more agile than the standard rocket launcher. Some sort of bomb radio car that drives along the ground. There seems to be both a fat and thin laser. You can even find alternate bombs like one that ignites the ground on fire. Each of the weapons has incredible impact and is fun to use; except the pistol.
To get weapons or items you need to save prisoners-of-war that will wave you over. Once you shoot or stab them, they'll be free to walk around and then when you touch them they'll pull up a pair of boxer shorts and reveal an item within. It sounds bizarre, but that's just the tip of the iceberg.
I always go out of my way to save every POW; no man left behind! They will amount to a bonus score at the end of the level, but only if you haven't died after saving them. One of them tries to help you out with some fancy moves from Street Fighter 2.
Like the other Metal Slug games for the PC, I have a feeling this is emulation. There's no way my beast of a computer would slow down from an arcade game from over fifteen years ago. Its designed to emulate that old Neo Geo feel, warts and all. Its nothing game breaking, but it is noticeable.
You'll find modernization here like achievements and a wide array of video options. There are controls for the keyboard or a 360 controller, but sadly, no mouse exclusive input where the middle mouse is the gun, the right button is the jump and the left button is the grenade. Such a missed opportunity there.
While the linear ride is over in an hour, that's still twice the time of the original Metal Slug. Its a great time for any arcade game and it leaves you wanting more. Lucky for you there are so many Metal Slugs.

People are giving this game bad reviews because there wasn't any major update.
But what they don't realise is that devs are releasing Nightly build (beta of beta).
Nightly build is nice feature because we can play with new features that aren't in game and maybe won't ever be.
Nightly build has some great features like new Novakid race , advanced combat, lot of new items, ship AI and way more stuff that is not yet in game.It's lot of fun after you run out of things to do in normal game.
But be warned!!! Nightly build is REALY BROKEN some times, it's beta version of beta version game so bugs, glitches and fps drops are expected.
Still a lot of fun to play in your free time, exploration is basicly infinite because of 5 sectors that have very large amount of solar systems that usually have around 3-4 planets so going over them all is pretty much impossible.
So for my conclusion:
Pros:
+6 playable races ,each with their own culture
+Lot of planets and solar systems to explore
+Lots of collectables (Horse head,outfits,playable musical instruments ...)
+Soundtrack is incredible
+Random types of enemies
+Techs (Dash, power jump, power ball from Metroid, Mech ...)
+Big selection of weapons and guns (guns can be optained on Avian ship that you find by finding big anchor on the ground)
+Armor (You will mostly use Racial armor but you can buy blueprints of armor of other races)
+Decoration (Lots of stuff for decoration, but you must find it first)
+Dungeons (Racial dungeons are designed by racial culture, like Avian Dungeon is designed to look really religious,Glitch have medieval castles with king and knights,Humans have prisons .... Oh and there is a Sewer Dungeon with poop enemies :D)
+Progression (You can progress in game by beating Bosses, crafting upgrades to be able to craft items with better ores)
+Mini-Bosses (Mini-bosses are randomly generated big enemies that are really powerful and are fairly challenging, but they drop rare items)
+Uncommon and Legendary Weapons (Rare weapons have special function like setting enemies on fire,poisoning them ect., Legendary weapons are signature like Tesla staff shooting lightning bolts....)
+When Floran (Plant people that are hunters) describe something it's usually pretty funny ("Fishface! Away!")
+Nightly build (It's broken, but fun)
+Stars falling at night look beautiful
+2D graphics looks nice in this game
Cons:
-Bosses (They are easy to beat if you wall yourself in and poke them with a stick through tiny space)
-Combat (Enemies are trying to ram into you, some have projectiles, some just charge) BUT!!! In Nightly build enemies AI is improved significantly and they are real danger to you.
-Fps drops sometimes but thats because of Beta or my computer :)
-Sometimes it's hard to get Nightly build to work
-Enemies are sometimes annoying (Like when you're climbing anchor to get to Avian ship and bird comes and knocks you down,DAMN YOU BIRD!!!)

I have been reading a lot of the supposed "most helpful reviews" and I must say I disagree strongly. Also, the fact that the "most helpful" review not only has a lower percentage of people who found it helpful, but has fewer people who voted on it period, means that something is drastically wrong with the reviews most people will see when they look at this game.
Now, many of the "most helpful" reviews have very outdated information. First off, the game is very much in full development mode, and the developers are adding in content by the bucket full, and revamping the game. The game already has a significant amount of content in it, and because of that, I find the fact that its developers say it's still not even close to finished very promising. Second, a lot of the reviews say that time stops when you go to other planets, this is NOT true at all anymore. The game has progressed a lot since most negative reviews have been written, and a lot of the things they say are either no longer true, or never were.
I find this game to only have a few things I would actually change about it:
The fact that all wood is "unrefined" and you don't get different kinds of wood from different trees. HOWEVER, there are about 200+ different kinds of trees, and the developers have already said they would eventually make all kinds of wood different.
The modding system leaves something to be desired, but it is very unfinished according to the developers, and it is already one of the best modding systems I've seen to date that actually don't restrict you in what you can do. It is written in lua, and can be easily decompiled using a tool they have already provided, meaning one can potentially use the system to make an entirely different game if they wanted to, and still have it launch from starbound's launcher.
Also, there is a good chance for save corruption, but the bug causing them to be corrupted is ALREADY FIXED in the latest nightly build. And, even when saves are corrupted, it is normally only the player's location that has changed, meaning that if you remember where you were before, you can easily return there.
I love this game, and I feel that it has a growing communiy, with tons of potential. On a final note, for the people who say this game is as easy as minecraft, I say I must disagree. While not as hard as Terraria can get, it is not as easy as unmodded minecraft, unless you play minecraft on hard, which is actually a challenge for some of us who have slowler computers.

Omsi 2 is a game that you cannot take seriously.
You can try, you can set up your fancy steering wheel, clip on your TrackIR, have the IBIS app on your mobile phone of choice, even wear a floppy hat, but when you get started, you learn that the AI is just too dumb to play it seriously.
So don't, and enjoy it.
Part of the fun is the mishaps that happen on the way, which there will be many. Under the hood the game is actually pretty darn great, good bus physics, and the sound design is just one of the best in gaming history (and that is no joke). Collision physics suck, mind. Well, they're great if you want to shoot your own bus, or another bus, into the stratosphere.
For the most part the quality of the content is good, very good in fact. Originally a tiny dev team it is clear that this was a labour of love, and that effort shows in the stock content and some of the DLC. SOME, not all. Very much like Dovetail, Aerosoft are willing to put any old map/vehicles on the Steam store to earn them some cash. This makes purchases very hit and miss, and finding reviews in a place other than Steam could be difficult. In general though, pretty good, and Omsi 2 has a great modding scene, some of which equal or even better the quality of official DLCS.
Omsi 2 is oddly engaging, and entertaining, and sort of falls into that realm of Farm Simulator or Eurotruck Simulator where really the game should be boring as hell, and maybe it is, but you still come back for more. There is a odd satisfaction of driving around a sleek, modern hybrid bus, or one of those real diesel smoke spewers of the 80s, you can practically smell the stubbed out cigarettes and that yellow liquid that could either be beer or urine or both.
What this game begs for is optimisation. The game engine of Omsi 2 is pretty much as good as it can get, DLC creators try their best to improve matters, but the core game itself could do with a proper polish up (pokes Aerosoft in the ribs, you listening?). I would love to see this in something like the Unreal Engine or Unity, doubt that would happen though. Any half decent rig should be able to make very few concessions in game settings, but don't expect constant 60s.
If you want to buy a few DLCs to expand on the stock content, the Berlin X10 is a great buy (huge map),  as is Hamburg. The forthcoming Omsi 2 Add On London DLC (formerly the mod called The South London Project) is one I'm very much looking forward to, not only to drive some iconic buses, but also to terrorise the streets of my nations capital.
A double decker doing scandinavian flicks around Marble Arch? Sign me up.

First, the bad:
The graphics, game engine and menus seem about 20 years old.
Poorly optimised - the framerate nosedives in certain areas.
Many, many bugs eg:
- Hold a button for a fraction of a second too long in the tutorial and it won't let you go back
- Then restarting the tutorial causes the game to crash
- Flip your bus and it falls through the road because the roof doesn't have a collision box
Serious localisation issues:
- Tutorials are written in very broken English
- During one of the tutorials, it tells you to press Shift+Z when you actually need to press Shift+Y (due to Germany using QWERTZ keyboards), and it won't let you proceed until you figure it out
- You are told to adjust a control in English, but they are all labelled in German. Tell us the German name as well, or at least provide tool-tips!
Controls:
- Despite claiming full joypad support, the joypad controls are far too sensitive; the slightest movement results in screeching tyres and complaining passengers. A separate program like Xpadder is required to use the more linear steering setup of the keyboard version.
- Some controls needlessly require separate on/off buttons to be mapped instead of a single toggle switch
Overpriced. You only get one map and a tiny tutorial map. Including more maps would make it a fairer price.
Good luck with getting through the poorly-translated, buggy tutorials and setting up the convoluted controls before your 2-hour refund window expires!
On the positive side, once the initial period of frustration is out of the way, it does provide a fairly satisfying in-depth simulation of bus driving. If you can overlook the many issues you should get some enjoyment out of it (you only need to look at the thousands of hours some of these other reviewers have ploughed into it to confirm that!), however it is very expensive and therefore I can only recommend it if this sort of thing really floats your boat. I played this game at a friends house on the console, and when the Steam Summer Sale started I picked this up at what I would consider a somewhat good deal. However, everything didn't go to plan and I ended up refunding the game pretty quickly, my short rundown...
The Good: For one, this game looks beautiful. One of the prettiest games I've ever seen, and the artistic style of the world, its inhabitants, and the gear are great. The performance was  also really good given the amount of visuals the game pushes. The gameplay itself (which strongly resembles the Demon/Dark Souls style) was also fun, with its own quirks compared to other games out there. I actually liked the leveling system for a game like this, and the interface (although not the most keyboard friendly) was really helpful telling me what I needed.
The Bad: As of June 16th, the day this was written, I just couldn't get over the crashes from this game. What's worse, when you crash you'll be left off the last save crystal you used. When a feature of the game is NOT to use them to build up a monster  multiplier for the equivalent of bonus XP, a crash is devastating. In addition, I noticed a ton of odd audio anomalies with the game. Voices were never a consistant volume, and it didn't seem audio positioning was done very well either. The voice acting of the game was...not so great, and the lip sync wasn't that great either. Your character's attitude seems a bit silly at times, and overall the story was a bit hit and miss.
I really want to like this game, and if it didn't have so many problems I think it could've been a really fun game. But my time in game was spent redoing everything I had just done due to crashes, coupled with the fact that the game didn't really seem to entice me to push the story forward, something the Souls series does fantastically.
At this time, I can't give a solid recommendation for the game, but it's definitely on my list of games to revisit in the future, because it seems like this could have good potential.

Summary: Hacknet is a fantastic hacker game; adding a terminal element sets it apart from other games in the genre such as Uplink: Hacker Elite. While in between storyline hacks the game leaves players feeling like their hacks have little reward or purpose, the stunning gameplay, visuals, and story make this game a must buy if you enjoy computers and being stressed out of your mind.
Hacking games such as this are always a thrill, at least in my experience. Nothing gets your heart racing more than a big red countdown as your fingers slip trying to type in a password. Hacknet is a great example of this genre.
Games such as Uplink: Hacker Elite have the player take part in "Hollywood hacking", using things like password crackers and dragging bypassers over network elements. While Hacknet it far from realistic hacking, the addition of the terminal makes the game so much better. While clicking and dragging can take time, it is far more stressful to type commands under pressure than it is to click them. This is one of Hacknet's biggest strengths, and players even have the ability to completely remove the user interface and play the game strictly through the terminal.
However, as I play Hacknet, there are periods of time where I'm not quite sure what I'm trying to acheive. I accept a contract, complete a hack, and at the end receive an email with a rank out of 100. This is where I think Uplink has the advantage; as you completed jobs you were paid money in order to upgrade you computer hardware and software. In Hacknet, the only time I really feel purposeful in my hacking in when I'm working on a hack relating to the story.
On top of great gameplay, the visuals of Hacknet are astounding. Just before writing this review I had a trace complete on me during a hack, and was greeting with the scariest red screen I've ever seen. The following sequence of trying to fix my mistake (I won't spoil anything!) was absolutely the most stressful thing I've experienced in a game.
Hacknet also has a great story (at least so far!), and I'm having trouble tearing myself away from the screen. All in all this game is a definite buy if you're into computers and having a heartrate of over 150.

------------------------------------- Old Review :( ---------------------------------------------------------------
From August, 2014
It has been roughly five or more months since I actually played Starbound. The reason is very simple: No updates or attempt from the developers to stage an update for us, the consumers looking for a finished game. When I first got the game in December I did enjoy the gameplay. I explored all the planets, races, and loot that the game had and built many buildings and structures. When I ran out of things to do I began modding the game, making my own modifications and finding others online. Finally, after 200+ hours of gameplay I decided to wait until the next update to continue playing. I would read through whatever updates the developers would give on their website and hope for something more to play, but now I am here, writing a review for a game I put a lot of time and hope into.
Honestly, I liked the gameplay. Simple and Terraria-like it was cute and fun, my favorite parts being looting and finding better guns and instruments to bring back to my extravagantly built bases. After I modded the game I would be doing the same thing, but in a spaceship of my own design. Sadly, the core game did not keep me entertained for the majority of the hours I have played and I quickly went on to learn how to modify my experience. As I continued to play I would simply lust for exploring to try and find something that I had yet to see, but to no avail. I think it says something when your favorite part of the game is the mods that you get or make for it.
After all this time I want to alert buyers that this “Early-Access Beta” game has little signs of coming out of it any time soon. Save your money and buy something similar, like Terraria, Minecraft, or another sandbox game offering more chances for adventure and creativity. On top of this the developer’s relationship with the community is poor and there are many other well written reviews explaining this issue.
In conclusion I do not recommend this game. However, my views may change if the developers manage push out an acceptable content update to explain the extensive delays (7 to 8 months worth), but sadly it may take another year for that to happen. I do wish for the game to see another release because I do love this game, a lot more than Terraria. I just hope I will be able to see it finished any time soon.

One of my all-time favourite games, if you love strategy games with plenty to manage and keep in mind, I couldn't recommend it enough. Currently having great fun discovering the amazing amount of extra content in the DLC, Crimson Court.
+Great artstyle.
+Great character/enemy concepts (DLC adds vampires based on mosquitoes, for example).
+Fantastic dynamic soundtrack that gets more intense as light levels drop, really adds to the atmosphere.
+Narrator Wayne June provides a jaw-droppingly satisfying performance.
+Tight inventory management, stress management, resource management, party management etc. Forces you to make tough but satisfying prioritisation decisions based on your situation.
+Game is IMO perfectly balanced so that you can make almost any situation work with enough skill and a maybe a lil luck. You can put your healer at the front of the group if you gear your party for that. If you think a class is bad, it's because you haven't used them enough.
While, yes, each area has maybe 20-30 distinct encounters that you will see time and again, each encounter is tailored to provide its own challenge in prioritisation based on who you're using, what attacks they have, which enemies are in what position, who ends up going before who, and what state your heroes are in at the time, among other subtle factors (phobias, buffs, debuffs, trinkets, etc etc). Having a team that can move the enemies out of position gives you much different options for strategy comparted to having a team that stuns well, for example.
I would definitely recommend skimming through a couple videos seeing how people prepare for different areas, and how well it goes. You can find detailed spreadsheets giving outlines for what to bring where. Youtuber Baertaffy has played this game so much, and at the start of his videos he explains who and what he's bringing where and why. Maybe watch the first few minutes of a handful of his DD videos to get an idea of how to prepare. If you're unsure on what to bring, overpreparation is a safe bet. Bring lots of food and shovels.

You'll see a lot of whining about the graphics and crashing issues in the reviews on this game. Not here. Personally, anything that crashes has fixes, it's the nature of PC gaming.
The reason I don't reccommend this game is because it's NOT a PC game.
It's a bad playstation port of what could otherwise be a wonderful game. However, the controls are set terribly to Keyboard & Mouse, and it offers -NO- reasonable tutorial. It pretends to offer a tutorial, but adds arbitrary labels to keys instead of telling you what key is assigned to a function, leaving you fumbling around in hopes of figuring out how to even attack. The only way to mitigate this is to actually go into the controls screen in the main menu options and read every. single. keybind.
On top of that, your mouse is not only useless, it will prevent you from playing the game. I actually had to take my hand -off- of the mouse to keep the game from tabbing out, because it minimized if I ever left or right clicked. To top it off, the camera isn't bound to any mouse functions, so there is absolutely no point to ever use your mouse for this game. Your keyboard is all of the controls, and it's even clumsier than a controller.
I found myself so frustrated with this game after just the first two missions, I had to quit. Maybe I'll come back with a controller when I'm craving a console experience, but if that was what they wanted to offer, BLADESTORM would have been better off staying on the Playstation.

Well, I did it. After 8 months of on and off playing, I finally completed the game and was greeted with that magnificent credits scroll. The satisfaction, relief and euphoria I felt after defeating the final boss of the game and seeing the credits reflected on the same emotions I had felt after beating every boss. Dark Souls 3 is a frustrating game. I can't tell you how many times I wanted to smash my controller to a pulp (believe me- you want to play this on a controller) and stop playing. I just couldn't bring myself to give up because of Pontiff Sulyvahn's atrociously long combos or the Nameless King's infinite stamina- the goal of finishing the game was all too alluring for me.
The only word I can describe dark souls perfectly with is "beautiful". The graphics and settings are simply stunning and painting-esque and each location along your arduous is uniquely coloured. The soundtrack works in tandem with the adventure, especially the last boss. The combat system is absolutely flawless and easy to learn, it's just a matter of mastering the parrying, rolling and dodging. There is a vast variety of weapon choices (my personal favourite is Yhorm's Great Machete) as well a smorgasbord of spells, allowing for ranged as well as melee combat. This is one of the reasons I love DS3- the player has many options and can play in any way they want to. In addition, the clever use of non-linear progression is a breath of fresh air from oddly linear open world games we see today.
The bosses in Dark Souls 3 are frustratingly difficult. Every boss is uniquely designed and presents a fresh challenge for players. My personal favourite boss was Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince because of the fact you had to basically fight two people, one could revive the other. However difficult the bosses may be, it's the satisfaction of spending hours on each one to finally defeat them, harvesting their souls and lighting their bonfires which makes each boss so rewarding.
Overall, Miyazaki as successfully crafted a stunning work of art and a brilliant game, a game which I highly recommend to anyone who enjoys challenges, fantasy and rich lore.

OVERALL: Expect your traditiional AC gameplay...in a world that is more realistic and lively than ever.
